item.title: Zurich Airport: record with 123'000 passengers
item.description: On Sunday, October 4, Zurich welcomed 123'000 travelers: a still-provisional record linked to the autumn school holidays in several German-speaking Swiss cantons.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 123'000 passengers in Zurich on a single Sunday - The October 4 figure is still provisional - Autumn holidays in several German-speaking Swiss cantons - Final figures expected in mid-November ## Key facts - What → passenger record in a single day - Where → Zurich Airport - When → Sunday, October 4 - How many → 123'000 travelers - Data status → still provisional - Explanation → autumn school holidays in several German-speaking Swiss cantons - Update → final figures in mid-November - History → first runway in operation since June 14, 1948 On Sunday, October 4, Zurich Airport welcomed 123'000 travelers, the highest number ever recorded in a single day at the airport. The operating company announced the figure, confirming a report published by Tages-Anzeiger. The record is not yet final. A spokesperson clarified that the available figures are provisional; the final count will be released in mid-November. The wording already limits the scope of the news: the record concerns a single Sunday and, for now, is based on a count that still needs to be completed. The operating company linked the high passenger numbers to the autumn school holidays that began in several German-speaking Swiss cantons. The source therefore indicates a specific reason for the concentration of travelers: the holiday calendar in part of German-speaking Switzerland. To interpret the record accurately, it must be kept tied to the stated day and to the provisional nature of the count. It is not a description of an entire period, but the result reported for that Sunday. ### An airport with a national history Zurich Airport is described as Switzerland's most important airport. Its origins date back to the period after the Second World War, when aviation activities were transferred from Dübendorf (ZH) to the airport. The historical reference does not alter the record figure for Sunday, but recalls how aviation activities were transferred from Dübendorf after the war. The first runway entered service on June 14, 1948. That day, a Swissair Douglas DC-4 four-engine aircraft took off for London. This separation is also useful when writing the news: the airport's history explains its origins, while the record indicates only the volume handled on that day according to the available data. ## How to read the Swiss mobility record The data has two coordinates that need to be considered together: Zurich Airport and Sunday, October 4. The first identifies Switzerland's most important airport; the second indicates that this is a daily measurement, not an assessment covering an entire season. For those who live or work in the country, the news therefore offers a concrete way of interpreting it: in this case, the high passenger volume is linked to the school vacation calendar, which began in several German-speaking Swiss cantons. ### A number to use with caution The 123'000 travelers describe the scale of the day indicated by the operating company. On their own, they do not make it possible to turn the record into a forecast for every Sunday, a measure of annual traffic, or a comparison with other airports. These extensions would go beyond the reported data. The same company referred to the figures as still provisional: until the final numbers are released in mid-November, the term record must remain tied to the provisional wording. The explanation must also remain limited. The high passenger volume was attributed to the autumn school vacations that began in several German-speaking Swiss cantons. The data suggests looking at the cantonal calendar when analyzing days of peak mobility, but does not authorize presenting the same dynamic as uniform throughout Switzerland. ### A reference for those organizing their travel The information can be paired with practical tools without attributing to the record effects that the source does not describe. To navigate the options of mezzi pubblici, it is advisable to keep the historical data and travel planning separate. Those who need to assess expenses in foreign currency can use comparatore CHF/EUR, without confusing this tool with a consequence announced by the airport. The central point remains the quality of the measurement: one day, one provisional figure, one reason linked to vacations in several cantons. The procedure does not change the source's content; it serves to ensure that the qualifications accompanying the data are not lost. 1. State the date. Write Sunday, October 4 and specify that it refers to a single day. The date prevents the record from becoming a generic reference to the airport's activity. 2. State the figure. Use the figure of 123'000 travelers welcomed by Zurich Airport. The word travelers should be linked to the airport and the stated day, not to an annual total. 3. State the status. Present the result as a record based on data that is still provisional. The spokesperson explained that the final count will be released in mid-November. 4. State the reported reason. Link the high turnout to the autumn school holidays that began in several German-speaking Swiss cantons, without expanding the explanation beyond what was communicated. ### Separate the data from the history If the news is accompanied by a fact sheet about the airport, it is advisable to keep the historical reference in a separate block. Zurich Airport was established after the Second World War with the transfer of aviation activities from Dübendorf (ZH). The first runway became operational on June 14, 1948; on that occasion, a four-engine Douglas DC-4 operated by Swissair took off for London. ### The final check In mid-November, when the final figures are released, the wording can be updated while keeping the date, quantity, and status of the data separate. ## TL;DR - The Schwyz UDC section proposes André Rüegsegger - First official candidacy after the announcement of the resignation - Rüegsegger has been a member of the Schwyz government since 2012 - The DFGP is indicated as a possible department ## Key facts - Candidate → André Rüegsegger - Party → UDC of the Canton of Schwyz - Age → 50 years old - Origin → Brunnen (SZ) - Cantonal government → since 2012 - Re-election in 2024 → second place, 37'989 votes - Department indicated → DFGP - First candidacy → after the announcement of the resignation at the end of the year The Schwyz section of the UDC has proposed State Councillor André Rüegsegger to the UDC's national search committee. It is the first official candidacy to emerge since President of the Confederation Guy Parmelin announced on Friday his intention to resign at the end of the year. The proposal comes from the Schwyz UDC section and is being presented to the national party as a candidacy to succeed outgoing Parmelin. Today's statement says that Rüegsegger has the ideal profile and age for the federal executive. Fifty years old, a native of Brunnen (SZ) and trained as a lawyer, Rüegsegger has been a member of the Schwyz government since 2012. Initially, he headed the Security Department; since 2020, he has been responsible for the Construction Department. In 2024, he was convincingly re-elected to the cantonal executive, finishing second overall with 37'989 votes. The report, however, concerns the proposal to the national committee, not a federal election result. The candidacy would also have a distinctive feature: Rüegsegger would be the first Federal Councillor from Schwyz in the federal executive. The source presents this as a possible first for the canton, alongside his biographical profile and experience in the Schwyz government. ### The political profile indicated by the party The UDC's cantonal president, Roman Bürgi, quoted in the statement, considers Rüegsegger particularly well suited to head the Federal Department of Justice and Police, the DFGP. At the Swiss UDC assembly in January 2025, Rüegsegger argued that the package should be submitted to a double majority of the people and the cantons. The comparison, therefore, concerns different backgrounds within the party. The second key is the possible department. Roman Bürgi identifies the FDJP as a suitable area for Rüegsegger; however, the source does not announce an allocation of departments. For the reader, this means distinguishing between an orientation expressed by the cantonal president and a federal decision that is not described. The significance of the candidacy is therefore political; the source does not report amounts or measures concerning costo della vita in Svizzera. The third key concerns agreements with the EU. The position expressed by Rüegsegger at the January 2025 assembly indicates his stance on the approval procedure: a double majority of the People and the Cantons. The text does not report the outcome of a vote on the package. The issue therefore remains an indicator of his political profile, not an outcome or decision already reported by the source. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the story For those living or working in Switzerland, following this candidacy means above all distinguishing the steps already documented from the decisions that have not yet been described. item.title: Fireworks, the right launches the no campaign against the initiative
item.description: Campaign against the fireworks initiative kicks off on Tuesday: the vote is on November 29. Centro, PLR, UDC and the business community support the no vote.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The opposing committee launched the campaign on Tuesday. - The vote on the initiative is scheduled for November 29. - The text concerns noise and emissions from fireworks. - Centro, PLR, UDC and the business community reject the ban. ## Key facts - Initiative → protection of people, animals and the environment - Vote → November 29 - Exceptions → large supra-regional events, at the discretion of the cantons - Opponents → Centro, PLR, UDC and the business community On Tuesday, the committee opposed to the fireworks initiative launched its campaign ahead of the November 29 vote. The message chosen to present the no vote is “What unites us must remain.” For the right wing and the business community, the campaign’s focus is the method: protection should not be entrusted to bans, but to responsibility. This position was made public by the committee opposed to the proposal. The text at the center of the debate was presented by organizations for the protection of animals. It calls for greater protection of people, animals and the environment from the noise and emissions caused by fireworks. The proposal therefore links the issue to the protection of three interests explicitly identified in the text: people, animals and the environment. ### What the text provides Alongside the call for greater protection, the proposal provides for some exceptions. They concern large supra-regional events, and the decision in these cases is left to the cantons. The exception is therefore not presented as automatic: the text gives the cantons discretion over whether it can be applied. The no camp brings together representatives of Centro, PLR and UDC, along with the business community. In a statement, they say they oppose a disproportionate nationwide ban. The objection concerns both private celebrations and events organized by associations or organizations: according to their position, both would suffer as a result. The campaign is defined by two approaches. On the one hand, the organizations promoting the initiative are calling for greater protection from noise and emissions, with exceptions for large supra-regional events left to the cantons. On the other, the opposing representatives and the business community reject the idea of a nationwide ban and call for a focus on responsibility. For the Swiss reader, the political point to follow is the distinction between a national rule and the exceptions left to the cantons. The November 29 vote will be the moment identified by the source for comparing these two positions, together with the consequences envisaged for private celebrations and organized events. The practical crux of the proposal emerges when distinguishing the contexts in which fireworks are used. The source does not treat them all in the same way: the no camp's statement mentions private parties and organized events, while the text of the initiative provides for an exception for major supraregional events. ### Three areas to distinguish | Area | What emerges from the source | |---|---| | Private parties | The opposing side argues that they would be affected. | | Events organized by associations or organizations | The statement lists them among the activities that would be affected by the national ban. | | Major supraregional events | The text provides for exceptions and leaves the decision to the cantons. | This distinction changes how the vote is read. For a private party, the comparison is between the greater protection sought by the initiative and criticism of a national ban. For an association or organization, the point is that the no camp considers its events potentially affected by the measure. For a major supraregional event, however, the text does not close off every possibility: it provides for an exception, but leaves it to the discretion of the cantons. The source expressly indicates cantonal discretion regarding exceptions for major supraregional events; it does not describe private parties or events organized by associations and organizations in the same way. For this reason, the role of the cantons is indicated in the passage on exceptions, while the position of representatives of Centro, PLR, UDC and the business community concerns the idea of a national ban considered disproportionate. The comparison thus sets out two different criteria. The first measures protection from noise and emissions for people, animals and the environment. The second assesses whether a national rule could affect private parties and association initiatives. The vivere in Svizzera guide offers a separate path for other issues of national life; here the focus remains the relationship between protection, responsibility and cantonal discretion. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. Before November 29, the reader can turn the text into a simple evaluation grid. The aim is not to add rules not present in the source, but to distinguish precisely between what the initiative is requesting and the response of the opposing committee. ### Four steps for reading the proposal 1. Set the objective: start from the request for greater protection for people, animals and the environment and connect it to the two effects indicated, noise and emissions from fireworks. 2. Separate the instrument: compare the request contained in the text with the no camp's position, which prefers responsibility over bans and rejects a national ban deemed disproportionate. 3. Classify the case: ask yourself whether the reference is a private party, an event organized by an association or a public body, or a large supraregional event. 4. Check the exception: for large supraregional events, the proposal indicates an exception, whose application is left to the discretion of the cantons. This sequence avoids two confusions. The first is mistaking the cantonal exception for a general freedom regarding every use of fireworks. The second is reading the proposal as if it concerned only large events, when the no campaign's statement also refers to private parties and events organized by associations or public bodies. The date to mark on the calendar is November 29, the date indicated for the vote. Before that day, the comparison sheet can remain anchored to three questions: what protection is being requested, which activities the opposing side considers exposed, and what space is left to the cantons. item.title: Unemployment insurance: loss of 249 million in 2025
item.description: The AD closes 2025 with a loss of 249 million: outflows of 8,69 billion, inflows of 8,44 billion and average unemployment at 2,8%.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - AD posts a loss of 249 million francs in 2025 - Average unemployment rises to 2,8% - Expenditure at 8,69 billion, revenue at 8,44 - Net equity falls to 7,96 billion ## Key facts - 2025 result → loss of 249 million francs - Average unemployed → 133'712 - Average rate → 2,8% - Expenditure → 8,69 billion francs - Revenue → 8,44 billion francs - Federal benefits cancelled → approximately 0,60 billion francs - Net equity → 7,96 billion francs - Formal approval of the accounts → still pending ## AD's 2025 accounts BERN - Unemployment insurance (AD) closed its 2025 accounts with a loss of 249 million francs. SECO announced the result together with the average unemployment rate, which rose to 2,8%. Expenditure amounted to 8,69 billion francs, while revenue reached 8,44 billion. The comparison with the previous year is stark: in 2024, AD had recorded a surplus of 1,43 billion. This shift from a positive result to a loss captures the change in the annual accounts between the two financial years. Expenditure in 2025 therefore exceeded revenue, as the figures released indicate. ### More people without work The average number of unemployed people rose from 112'563 in 2024 to 133'712 in 2025. The unemployment rate increased by 0,4 percentage points, reaching 2,8%. SECO defines this figure as being in line with the long-term average. The two elements are presented together: the average number of people without work and the average rate recorded during the year. The result was particularly affected by the cancellation of the Confederation's benefits to AD, amounting to approximately 0,60 billion francs. The measure is part of a package of financial and administrative relief measures. The source therefore links the loss both to the trend in unemployment and to the cancellation of federal benefits. Following the loss, the net equity of the AD compensation fund fell to 7,96 billion francs at the end of 2025. The Swiss Federal Audit Office has completed the audit, but formal approval of the annual accounts by the Federal Council is still pending. For the reader, distinguishing between the annual accounts, the unemployment indicator and the fund's capital makes it possible to follow the three reported figures separately. Anyone looking for a new job can read this alongside annunci di lavoro. ## The comparison that emerges from the figures The shift from a surplus to a loss is the first element to observe, but it does not exhaust the reading of the accounts. The published data set out three different aspects side by side: how many people are unemployed on average, how much flows into and out of the AD, and what net equity remains at the end of 2025. Keeping them separate avoids treating a labor-market statistic and a balance-sheet item as equivalent. ### 2024 and 2025 compared | Indicator | 2024 | 2025 | |---|---:|---:| | Average number of unemployed | 112'563 | 133'712 | | AD result | Surplus of 1,43 billion | Loss of 249 million | The table shows the change in direction of the result and the increase in the average number of unemployed. However, these are not the same type of measure: the first figure concerns the AD's accounts, while the second describes the average number of people unemployed during the year. The 2025 average rate, at 2,8%, is stated by SECO to have risen by 0,4 percentage points and to be in line with the long-term average. This wording offers two ways of reading it: on the one hand, it records an increase compared with the previous year; on the other, it places the figure in the historical perspective invoked by SECO itself. ### Flows, equity and federal benefits Outflows of 8,69 billion and inflows of 8,44 billion are flows in the 2025 accounts. The cancellation of approximately 0,60 billion in federal benefits is instead indicated as a factor that weighed on the result, as part of a package of financial and administrative relief measures. The net equity of 7,96 billion ultimately captures the fund's position at the end of the year. It is therefore a figure to be read separately from the annual result. To organize a personal comparison of income, calcolatore stipendio remains a tool distinct from the AD's accounts and the average data reported by SECO. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## Four steps for consulting the data To turn the press release into a clear reading sheet, it is advisable to proceed step by step and keep the figures separate. 1. Start with the scope: note that these are the 2025 accounts of unemployment insurance and that the result was announced by SECO. 2. Separate the flows: record on two lines the expenditures, amounting to 8,69 billion francs, and the revenues, amounting to 8,44 billion. The reported result is a loss of 249 million. 3. Add the labor-market indicators: enter the average number of unemployed, 133'712, and the average rate of 2,8%, up by 0,4 percentage points. 4. Finish with the fund's position: add net equity of 7,96 billion at the end of 2025, then note that the audit by the Swiss Federal Audit Office is complete, while formal approval of the accounts by the Federal Council is pending. ### The final check The final check consists of not mixing the year's result with the fund's balance. The loss of 249 million concerns the 2025 accounts; the 7,96 billion concerns net equity at the end of the same year. The 2,8% rate and the average 133'712 unemployed people are also indicators distinct from the accounting items. This structure makes it possible to update one's sheet when new data become available, without confusing revenues, expenditures, average unemployment and capital. To complement the reading of personal income, the guide to busta paga svizzera is also available, separate from the unemployment insurance figures. To move from the general data to your own situation, use calcolatore stipendio. *Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/economia/1955004/disoccupazione-perdita-assicurazione-franchi-miliardi)*

item.title: Army strength is sufficient now but will fall by 2030
item.description: As of March 1, 2026, the army numbers 147 017 personnel, enough for the statutory 100 000, but a decline below 130 000 is expected by 2030.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 147,017 soldiers enlisted as of March 1, 2026 - A decline below 130,000 units is expected by 2030 - Soldiers available for training: +2.5% ## Key facts - Reference date → March 1, 2026 - Publication → October 6, 2026 - Soldiers enlisted → 147,017 - Regular strength → 100,000 soldiers - Forecast by 2030 → 130,000 units - Change in training → +2.5% - Expected popular vote → 2028 On October 6, 2026, in Bern, the 2026 Army Census was published. The survey photographs the forces as of March 1, 2026 and indicates that the formations today have a sufficient number of soldiers for the army to deliver its performance. ### A snapshot as of March 1 The total is 147,017 soldiers enlisted in the formations. The number is enough to guarantee, in case of deployment, the regular strength of 100,000 soldiers. The picture changes on the 2030 horizon: the strength should drop to 130,000 units. The shift is linked to the discharge from service in 2028 and 2029 of the last two age classes subject to a 12‑year mandatory military service. A short‑term indicator instead offers a positive signal. The number of soldiers available for ongoing training has increased by 2.5% compared to the previous year, with a particularly positive effect on the effective numbers of repeat courses. In recruitment the picture is mixed. The total number of recruitments is falling, while the number of female soldiers still grows slightly. The source links this trend to the great interest that women continue to show for a career in the officer corps, which entails a longer mandatory military service, and considers a further slight increase possible. The Federal Council adopted the related message in the session of September 9, 2026. The proposal to introduce a mandatory information day for women will now go to Parliament; the related popular vote should take place in 2028. With the current 70 percent eligibility rate for military service and moderate demographic growth among those subject to the obligation to serve, it would be possible to guarantee the recruitment of new recruits. However, almost 12,000 people subject to the obligation leave service early, especially for civil service. The indicated answer is greater flexibility of training and career models. In 2025 Parliament instructed the Federal Council to implement the «obligation to provide security service» to ensure personnel for the army and civil protection. On June 24, 2026 the Federal Council defined the reference parameters; consultation of the Cantons is underway. ## The challenge is the personnel timeline The news distinguishes between two levels: the army's current ability to deliver its services and personnel availability in future years. For those living or working in Switzerland, the practical takeaway is to distinguish the current situation from forecasts and measures still undergoing an institutional process. ### Three horizons not to be confused | Horizon | Indicated element | Practical reading | |---|---|---| | Today | Services guaranteed with available personnel | The data describes current capacity. | | 2028-2029 | Discharge of the last two age classes | This transition is cited as a factor in the decline. | | By 2030 | Projected personnel at 130,000 units | This is a projection, not a count at the time of publication. | | Institutional process | Message, Parliament, and consultation of the Cantons | The outcome is not yet described as final. | The 2.5% increase in personnel available for training does not offset the projected trajectory through 2030. These two data points measure different aspects: the first relates to current training compared to the previous year, with a positive impact particularly on refresher courses; the second concerns the evolution of overall personnel following the discharge of the last age classes under a 12-year obligation. The growth in the number of female soldiers also unfolds in two stages. Interest in leadership careers is already noted as a positive factor, while the mandatory information day is still part of a message adopted by the Federal Council and submitted to Parliament. A popular vote is expected to take place in 2028; therefore, its outcome cannot be treated as a settled decision. The nearly 12,000 early departures show that the issue is not solely about recruiting new members. Retention within the system is another factor noted by the source, particularly regarding the shift to civil service. More flexible training and career models are mentioned as a solution, but the press release does not yet specify how they will function, who will be eligible, or when they will take effect. The 'obligation to provide security service' follows a separate path: the parliamentary mandate dates back to 2025, the Federal Council's parameters were set on June 24, 2026, and the consultation with the Cantons is still ongoing. The press release does not provide a final text or a new individual deadline. Those interested in the professional side can supplement this information with job advertisements, without treating that catalog as census data. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to follow the dossier To read the updates without confusing numbers, forecasts, and decisions, it's best to use a simple sequence. ### The sequence to follow - Start from the reference date. The 2026 Army Census captures the actual numbers as of March 1, 2026, while the publication date is October 6, 2026. These two dates describe different moments. - Separate the actual strength from the regulatory strength. The first indicates the military personnel present in the formations; the second is the level of 100,000 military personnel to be guaranteed in case of deployment. This distinction helps to correctly understand any subsequent communications. - Keep the 2028 and 2029 calendars separate from the forecast for 2030. The first two dates concern the discharge of the last age groups with a 12-year military service obligation; 2030 is the horizon indicated for the expected strength. - Follow the path of the mandatory information day for women. The message was adopted by the Federal Council on September 9, 2026, must be submitted to Parliament, and the popular vote should take place in 2028. Until the process is completed, the proposal should not be presented as a definitive rule. - Check the progress of the "security service obligation." Parliament tasked the Federal Council in 2025, the reference parameters were defined on June 24, 2026, and the consultation with the cantons is underway. The source does not yet describe the individual effects of a possible final model. For those subject to the "service obligation," the press release provides useful indicators but does not list forms, questions to be submitted, or personal deadlines. The 70% suitability rate, the nearly 12,000 early departures, and the intention to make training and career models more flexible help to follow the topic, but do not replace any future instructions. The professional plan can be kept separate from the strength count: to explore available opportunities, you can consult the hiring companies, while the census remains the reference for army data. The news contains no information on salaries or taxes. For a separate economic comparison, use the salary calculator. *Source: [admin.ch](https://www.admin.ch/it/newnsb/TJk4QYGofEV-)*

item.title: The labor market situation in September 2026
item.description: In September 2026, Switzerland recorded 140’480 unemployed people, with the rate steady at 3%. This represents a monthly decrease of 0,8%, but an annual increase of 5,4%. There were 44’199 vacancies at the URCs.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - September: 140’480 unemployed people, unemployment rate at 3%. - Monthly unemployed down 0,8%. - Year on year, unemployed up 5,4%. - URC vacancies: 44’199, +1,1% month on month. ## Key facts - Source → SECO - Publication date → October 6, 2026 - Location → Bern - Period covered → September 2026 - Unemployed → 140’480 people - Unemployment rate → 3,0% - Seasonally adjusted unemployed → 147’411 people - Vacancies at the URC offices → 44’199 SECO published the latest findings on the labor market situation in Switzerland on October 6, 2026. The release, dated Bern, captures September 2026: there were 140’480 unemployed people, 1’064 fewer than in the previous month, equivalent to -0,8%, but 7’247 more than in the same month of the previous year, i.e. +5,4%. The unemployment rate remained unchanged at 3% (3,0% in the text). The seasonally adjusted number decreased by 475 units, or -0,3%, to 147’411 people; the seasonally adjusted rate remained at 3,1%. The release therefore distinguishes the regular monthly series from the one adjusted for seasonal variations, keeping both the counts and the rates separate. Overall, the release thus presents the situation from two perspectives: the figure observed in the month and the one adjusted for seasonality. The age groups and the group of people seeking employment are then indicated with their own figures and rates. Between August and September 2026, the number of unemployed young people aged 15 to 24 fell by 332 people (-2,3%), to 14’346. Year on year, however, there were 485 more people (+3,5%). The youth unemployment rate decreased by 0,1 percentage points, to 3,3%. For older workers, the monthly decrease was 201 people, or -0,5%, for a total of 38’482. Compared with the previous year, the increase was 2’291 people (+6,3%). The rate for the 50-64 age group was 2,6%, down by 0,1 points. ### The group of people seeking employment The separate category of people seeking employment comprises 227’592 people, 344 more than in the previous month (+0,2%) and 13’842 more than a year earlier (+6,5%). The rate remained at 4,8%. Adjusted for seasonal variations, the number instead fell by 444 units (-0,2%), to 237’244, with the rate unchanged at 5% (5,0% in the text). The distinction between these series makes it possible to view the monthly movement and the year-on-year comparison separately. To complement the general statistics with the published opportunities, the reader can consult annunci di lavoro. The figures on the exhaustion of entitlement to unemployment benefits are published with a delay. At the end of September 2026, the available data concerned cases from July 2026: 2’990 people, 254 more than in June, an increase of 9,3%. Payment practices mean that unemployment funds publish these cases with a two-month delay; the source specifies that the figures may still change. To interpret the figure correctly, July should not be mistaken for September. ### Vacancies at the URCs In September 2026, the URCs recorded 44’199 vacancies, 466 more than in the previous month (+1,1%). Of these, 29’251, or 66,2%, were subject to the reporting requirement. Compared with the same period of the previous year, the number of vacancies counted was 6’827 higher (+18,3%). The seasonally adjusted figure provides another perspective: 42’931 vacancies, 150 more (+0,4%) than in the previous month. For those seeking opportunities, the total number and the share subject to the reporting requirement are not the same information. The former indicates all vacancies reported to the URCs; the latter isolates part of that total. The monthly comparison, the annual comparison and the seasonally adjusted series should therefore be kept distinct. The link to aziende che assumono can support the interpretation without replacing the SECO figures. ### Short-time work: a more lagged snapshot The short-time work data available at the end of September refer to June 2026. There were 8’339 people affected, 84 fewer than in May, a decrease of 1% (the press release reports -1,0%), calculated over a three-month registration period. The businesses involved numbered 638, i.e. 35 more (+5,8%). Here too, the reference date is decisive. Counting and payment practices result in a three-month delay in the publication of counted cases; the figures may still change. The source's stated experience is that the short-time work counted and recorded after three months is around 75 per cent. For a reader, this means using June as the month of measurement and September as the point when the data became available. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. Anyone who wants to use the press release as an operational reference must start with the dates, not just the figures. The source gathers indicators covering different periods and points out delays related to payment or counting. An orderly reading prevents attributing to September data that refer to July or June. ### Five-step reading procedure 1. Pin down the date of the document. The SECO press release was published on October 6, 2026. The attached PDFs are dated October 5, 2026. These are publication dates: they must not be confused with the statistical period observed. 2. Indicate the reference period. For the main section, note September 2026. For the exhaustion of entitlement to unemployment benefits, note July 2026; for short-time work, June 2026. The different timing is part of the data. 3. Keep the categories separate. Unemployed people, seasonally adjusted unemployed people, young people aged 15 to 24, older workers aged 50 to 64 and people seeking employment are reported as separate entries. Keep the corresponding count and, where present, the corresponding rate for each. 4. Write down the type of comparison. Next to each value, indicate whether the change concerns the previous month, the same month of the previous year or the figure adjusted for seasonal variations. This note prevents putting changes that answer different questions on the same footing. 5. Treat vacancies and delayed data separately. For the URCs, retain the announced total, the share subject to the reporting obligation and the seasonally adjusted figure. For the exhaustion of entitlement to benefits and short-time work, add the publication delay and remember that the figures may change. This procedure does not modify SECO’s data: it makes them readable in their chronological order. The two PDFs can be placed alongside the press release to verify the document title and the associated date, while the page for annunci di lavoro offers an operational step for anyone who wants to look for opportunities without confusing the statistical data with the individual case. To move from general reading to personal comparison, use calcolatore stipendio. *Source: [admin.ch](https://www.admin.ch/it/newnsb/Cdju9-o8WGML)*

item.title: Health insurance premiums on the rise: heading toward 1000 francs a month
item.description: Next year, the average premium will be 488 francs (+23, +5%); in 14 years it could reach 966,20 francs if the 5% annual trend continues.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Next year, an average of 488 francs per month per adult - Increase of 5%, i.e. 23 francs more - 966.20 francs per month in the 14-year projection - If costs rise by 5%, premiums more than doubled by 2040 ## Key facts - Average amount for adults → 488 francs per month - Increase next year → 5%, equal to 23 francs - Projection → 966.20 francs after 14 years - Horizon → 2040 - Expert → Tilman Slembeck, ZHAW - Factors indicated → demographics, principle of trust, reforms Next year, adults will pay an average of 488 francs per month for compulsory basic health insurance. The increase will be 5%, equal to 23 francs more than today. The figure is an average, but it captures the pressure that health insurance premiums exert on the monthly budget. In just over 20 years, spending on compulsory basic health insurance has almost doubled. The new projection starts from this trend: if premiums continue to grow by an average of 5% per year, the current monthly premium would reach double, 966.20 francs, in just 14 years. For those who have to plan the cost of cassa malati, the figure indicates a long-term scenario, not an amount that has already been decided. ### The projection and its conditions The mathematical correctness of the calculation was acknowledged by Tilman Slembeck, a health economist at Zurich University of Applied Sciences, ZHAW. Contacted by 20 Minuten, he nevertheless pointed out that the financing of the healthcare system is undergoing restructuring. For this reason, it is not clear how rising costs will affect the future development of premiums. > “Mathematically, it is correct,” says Slembeck. Overall, the expert nevertheless expects an annual percentage increase in costs of 5% or more. If this trend were to continue, adult premiums would have more than doubled by 2040 compared with today. The direction indicated by the source is therefore clear: the situation would not become more affordable. Slembeck attributes the increases to several factors. The baby boom generation is aging; the principle of trust regarding services prescribed by doctors also has an impact. He adds to these factors the lack of any genuine political will to reform the system. In his view, reforms are difficult because the system’s stakeholders are well settled and profit from it, while those who pay the premiums and taxes remain excluded. The value of 488 francs becomes concrete when it enters the monthly budget. The source does not describe the premium as a problem limited to people in financial difficulty: Philipp Frei, director of the umbrella association Consulenza Budget Svizzera, says that the pressure also affects the middle class and weighs especially on families. His point concerns the money that remains available: people already have less money at their disposal each year and experience premiums as a burden. ### The bill does not end with the premium The average increase of 23 francs does not exhaust healthcare spending. On top of the premium come the deductible and everything not covered by health insurance. A budget that records only the monthly amount therefore does not reflect the full burden borne by those who have to pay for care. For a family, the difference between the premium, deductible and excluded services is not an accounting detail: it is the concrete measure of the money that may be lacking for other necessities. The issue is therefore also connected to costo della vita, and not only to the insurance line item. When resources shrink, the choice is no longer just how much to spend, but also which treatments to postpone. Frei says he knows many people who have not gone to the doctor or dentist for years because they cannot afford the care. Postponement leaves illnesses untreated and can make the situation more costly for the individual and for society as a whole. The source also notes that, already today, some people are excluded from the healthcare system because of high premiums. ### A problem that goes beyond income The practical consequence is that the increase does not affect just one group. People experiencing financial difficulties are affected, but the pressure also concerns the middle class; for families, Frei describes it as a major burden. The 5% used in the projection should therefore be read as potential pressure on household budgets, not as a figure to be applied automatically to every household. The financing system is undergoing restructuring, and the future relationship between costs and premiums remains uncertain: this condition prevents the projection from being treated as an invoice already written. For the reader, the practical check consists of looking at available money, the premium, deductible, uncovered services and postponed care together. These are the items that show whether the increase remains manageable or leads to foregoing medical care. To learn more about the insurance aspect, one can consult cassa malati. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ### A four-step check 1. Record the monthly premium paid today. The personal figure must be kept distinct from the average indicated for adults: 488 francs per month is the average benchmark for next year, not a figure presented as identical for every policyholder. 2. Isolate the average increase. The 23 francs represent the difference between next year's average and today's average. They help show the order of magnitude of the increase, but do not automatically justify treating the figure as the change in one's own bill. 3. Add the items not included in the premium. The budget sheet must also include the deductible and services not covered by health insurance. These are the two elements that the source indicates together with the premium when describing the overall burden of healthcare. 4. Prepare two time-based scenarios. The first uses the mathematical projection of 966.20 francs per month after 14 years, if average growth remains at 5% per year. The second considers 2040: with costs rising by 5% or more, adult premiums would have more than doubled compared with today. Both scenarios should be marked as hypotheses, because healthcare system financing is being restructured and the effect on premiums is unclear. ### Also record what people forgo The check should not stop at figures already paid. If a person has been putting off seeing a doctor or dentist for years because they cannot afford treatment, that sacrifice is part of the problem described by Philipp Frei. Recording it makes it possible not to confuse an avoided expense with a cost that has disappeared: according to the source, neglected illnesses can become more expensive for the person and for society. It is also the starting point for understanding the exclusion from the healthcare system reported for some people. The process does not produce a certain forecast: it organizes the available data and separates the average premium from the other expenses. To turn this check into a dedicated assessment, use our tool on cassa malati. *Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/economia/1954942/premi-anni-aumento-diventera-afferma)*

item.title: Ostinelli does not pay his health insurance and goes before the magistrate
item.description: Roberto Ostinelli, a doctor from Mendrisio, has not paid his health insurance since June 2024 and must appear before the magistrate on October 6; he pays 140 euro per month for international insurance.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Roberto Ostinelli has not paid his health insurance since June 2024 - The doctor from Mendrisio must appear before the magistrate on October 6 - International insurance costs 140 euros a month - The political proposal concerns a three-year period for people from Ticino ## Key facts - Person → Roberto Ostinelli, doctor and member of parliament from Mendrisio - Last payment → June 2024 - Hearing → Tuesday, October 6, before the magistrate - Alternative coverage → international insurance - Stated premium → 140 euros a month - Proposal → foreign insurance for people from Ticino for three years June 2024 was the last month in which Roberto Ostinelli, a doctor from Mendrisio, paid his health insurance. Since then, the bills have piled up, and on Tuesday, October 6, he will have to appear before the magistrate. The case concerns a cassa malati Swiss insurance policy and a choice that the person directly involved presents as voluntary and deliberate. During the Covid-19 pandemic, Ostinelli attracted attention with his unconventional views. He says that, like many people from Ticino and due to family problems, he experienced a difficult financial period: he knows what it means to make it to the end of the month and ask for an extension to pay a bill. To reduce expenses, he looked for another solution and found international insurance. He says he also has a foothold abroad, which would have allowed him to take it out. He was told that the coverage is valid throughout Europe, including Switzerland, and on other continents as well. The stated cost is 140 euros per month, one third of the cost of Swiss coverage. So far, he has paid for it without using it, because he has always been healthy and has a high deductible. The Swiss health insurance bills, however, continued to arrive. Initially, the doctor tried to reach an agreement with the health insurer, without success; his cancellation was not accepted. He therefore decided not to pay. He does not know what the outcome in court will be and speculates that he may be notified of a bankruptcy petition. > «Mine is a voluntary choice. A deliberate one. I want to send a message to the system». Ostinelli says that he does not consider himself a rebel and that his choice is not born of a whim: he invokes his own ethics and morality. His stated position is clear: whatever amount he is presented with, he will not pay it. ### The political proposal The doctor, who is also a member of parliament, would like the canton to consider allowing people from Ticino, for a three-year period, to take out foreign insurance. He acknowledges that most people cannot have a foothold outside Switzerland and that his concept conflicts with federal law. For this reason, he speaks of mediation with the insurance companies and announces that a sustainable health insurance model will come later. His proposal, he explained, should give those in difficulty some breathing room, without turning the choice into a mere provocation. ## The premium is not enough For those living in Switzerland, the case opens up a discussion that goes beyond converting euros into francs. LAMal/KVG is mandatory health insurance for residents: international coverage must therefore be assessed together with the insurance obligation, not only the stated monthly premium. In Ostinelli's case, a policy described as also being valid in Switzerland did not result in the Swiss insurer accepting the cancellation. The practical picture can be viewed on three levels: | Level | Element that emerged | What it indicates | | Cost | 140 euro per month, one third of Swiss coverage | It is the savings declared by Ostinelli, not a general measure of the protection | | Coverage | Europe, including Switzerland, and other continents | The geographic scope refers to his insurance | | Rules | Cancellation not accepted and conflict with federal law | The process does not end with the signing of a new contract | Differences between cantons matter because premiums are organized by canton or region and premium reductions are cantonal. For this reason, pressure on costo della vita in Svizzera is not addressed in the same way everywhere. ## TL;DR - Single-family homes: asking prices down 0.1% - Apartments: asking prices up 0.2% - Zurich: house prices down 2.7%, the sharpest decline - Condominiums: increases in Ticino and the Lake Geneva region
- Analysis → Immoscout real estate listings in collaboration with IAZI - Period → September, compared with August - Subject → asking prices set by sellers - Single-family homes → down 0.1% - Apartments → up 0.2% - Sharpest decline in house prices → Zurich, 2.7% - Condominiums → increases in Ticino, the Lake Geneva region, Northwestern and Central Switzerland
In Zurich, the September snapshot of residential properties for sale shows substantial stability across Switzerland, at least on a monthly basis. The data come from an analysis of real estate listings published by the Immoscout platform in collaboration with real estate consultancy IAZI. The survey looks at asking prices set by sellers and distinguishes between single-family homes and apartments.
The first segment recorded a decline of 0.1% compared with August. For apartments, on the other hand, prices rose by 0.2%. The comparison is therefore between two movements in opposite directions, although within an overall picture defined as substantially stable.
### The regional map of houses
The Swiss figure is not repeated in the same way in all regions. For single-family homes, the sharpest decline was recorded in Zurich, where the drop was 2.7%. Decreases were also recorded in the Mittelland, Central Switzerland and Ticino. Increases, on the other hand, concerned the Lake Geneva region, Eastern Switzerland and Northwestern Switzerland.
Condominiums follow a different distribution. Prices rose in Ticino, Northwestern Switzerland, the Lake Geneva region and Central Switzerland. They fell instead in Zurich and Eastern Switzerland.
This dual reading is the central point of the analysis: the national monthly direction is not enough to describe every area. The result changes when moving from single-family homes to condominiums and when shifting the observation between Zurich, Ticino, the Lake Geneva region and the other regions mentioned. For this reason, the figures should be read while keeping the type of property, the location and the comparison between September and August separate. The geographical reference is not a secondary detail, because the source records increases and declines in the same categories depending on the area considered. The distinction is therefore an integral part of the monthly data. This is not a single uniform movement. ### Two filters to avoid confusing the data
The national stability indicated for September is a starting point, not a figure to apply indiscriminately to every listing. The source cross-references two variables: the type of property and the region. A correct reading must retain both until the end of the comparison.
| Segment | Areas with declines | Areas with increases | | --- | --- | --- | | Single-family homes | Zurich, Swiss Plateau, Central Switzerland, Ticino | Lake Geneva region, Eastern Switzerland, Northwestern Switzerland | | Condominiums | Zurich, Eastern Switzerland | Ticino, Northwestern Switzerland, Lake Geneva region, Central Switzerland |
The table highlights a useful difference for anyone monitoring an asking price. In the single-family home segment, Ticino is among the areas experiencing a decline; in condominiums, by contrast, it is among those experiencing an increase. Zurich appears among the declining areas for both categories, while Eastern Switzerland shifts from an increase for single-family homes to a decline for condominiums. Northwestern Switzerland is increasing for both categories; Central Switzerland changes sign, with a decline for single-family homes and an increase for condominiums.
The correct reference remains the seller's asking price in the listing. This does not mean the data should be read as a single change for all homes: the monthly comparison is between September and August, and the regions are moving in different directions. If you take a listing, it is therefore advisable to note the category and area first, then check which row of the table corresponds.
To connect this reading to one's personal finances, without mixing different indicators, you can consult costo della vita in Svizzera. The link serves to broaden the reading, while the figures in the analysis remain confined to real-estate listings and the two categories described.
A comparison between two listings will therefore be consistent only if the data are reported in the same order: September, August, category, region, and asking price. If one of these coordinates is missing, the number loses its comparative meaning. The aim is not to turn a national change into an undifferentiated average, but to read the value in the combination indicated by the source.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ### Four operational checks
The data collection can be turned into a simple sheet. The objective is not to add estimates, but to keep the scope of the data intact: listings, asking prices, September, comparison with August, category and region.
1. Define the category. Indicate whether it concerns a single-family house or a condominium. Do not combine the two entries into a single row, because the source records different trends.
2. Indicate the region. Report the area associated with the listing: Zurich, Mittelland, Central Switzerland, Ticino, Lake Geneva region, Eastern Switzerland or Northwestern Switzerland. The location determines which regional comparison to use.
3. Set the time frame. Write September as the period observed and August as the monthly reference. This keeps the comparison tied to the interval indicated by the analysis.
4. Transcribe the reference. Keep the seller's asking price in the listing and do not replace it with a generic value. The subject of the price is also part of the interpretation.
After this recording, use the corresponding change without transferring it to another category. The 0,1% concerns single-family houses compared with August; the 0,2% concerns apartments. The 2,7% identifies the sharpest decline in house prices, in Zurich. These are three different references and must be kept in their respective boxes.
The sheet should also retain the source information: the listing analysis is published by Immoscout with IAZI and concerns sellers' asking prices. This way, the reader does not lose the meaning of the number when comparing it with a different figure.
A final check consists of rereading the regional row: for houses, do not confuse the decline in Ticino with the rise in the Lake Geneva region; for condominiums, do not confuse the rise in Ticino with the decline in Zurich. The source provides precisely this distinction, and preserving it prevents a comparison based solely on the national headline.
If the personal assessment requires an additional step concerning income, the website also offers busta paga svizzera. It is a separate analysis: it does not replace the real-estate data, but helps keep the asking price and one's own financial information distinct.

It may be mandatory or organized differently depending on the canton. For anyone managing a property in the Canton of Bern, the first practical step is to identify the applicable cantonal arrangement, not look for a national rate. The question falls into two parts. On the one hand, it must be verified whether the coverage falls under a requirement provided for that canton; on the other, which entity manages it. The section dedicated to Bern contemplates two possibilities: a cantonal authority or an authorized insurer. This distinction guides both requests for information and the interpretation of premiums and coverage. The premium should therefore be checked through the official cantonal channel, not automatically transferred from another canton. The verification must include requirements, amounts, deadlines and the claims procedure for the applicable channel. ### The tax framework remains separate To correctly assess costs related to the home, insurance must be kept separate from taxes. The Swiss tax system has three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; in municipalities, the multiplier is applied to the cantonal tax. AFC/ESTV handles direct federal tax and VAT, while cantonal administrations manage cantonal and municipal taxation. These responsibilities do not indicate which entity should manage building insurance in Bern. Anyone preparing dichiarazione delle imposte should therefore keep the tax item separate from the insurance premium. This distinction does not change the practical objective: understanding which rule applies to the property and which office or insurer provides the guidance. The data to use is not a national average, but the data linked to the applicable cantonal organization. The same criterion applies to the terminology. Requirement, authority, authorized insurer, coverage, premium and claim are different steps in the same verification. Treating them as synonyms may lead to seeking the right data through the wrong channel. For Bern, the guide therefore starts with the cantonal rule and only then addresses the expense and procedure. The practical issue is not only knowing whether an obligation exists. It is understanding through which mechanism the expense enters the budget. The Cantons do not have a single system, while the word premium appears in several Swiss contexts but does not mean the same thing. To avoid conflating building insurance, health coverage, pension provision and taxation, it is advisable to read the rules in parallel, without substituting one for another. ### Four mechanisms not to mix | Item | Stated rule | Practical reading | |---|---|---| | Building insurance | Obligation or different organization depending on the canton | Check the channel provided for in Bern | | LAMal/KVG | Mandatory for residents, to be taken out within 3 months of arrival | Per-capita premium; amounts by canton or region; cantonal premium reduction | | AVS/AHV, AI and IPG | 5.3% paid by the employee, 10.6% in total with the employer | Contribution based on salary | | LPP/BVG | 7%, 10%, 15% and 18% of coordinated salary | Age brackets 25–34, 35–44, 45–54 and 55+ until reference age | The comparison with LAMal/KVG serves to avoid using a health insurance premium as a reference for a building. LAMal is mandatory for residents, has per-capita premiums and provides for a premium reduction managed at cantonal level. Building insurance, on the other hand, follows the structure established by the canton: the correct comparison starts with the cantonal body or authorized insurer indicated for Bern. The payslip also uses a different mechanism. AVS/AHV, AI and IPG contributions amount to 5.3% for the employee and 10.6% in total with the employer. LPP/BVG applied to coordinated salary provides for 7% between ages 25 and 34, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54 and 18% from age 55 until reference age. These percentages are not building premiums. For taxes, the reference remains the division between federal, cantonal and municipal levels. UFAS/BSV concerns social security, including AVS, AI and LPP, and does not set taxes; UST/BFS produces statistics and does not set rates. This map of responsibilities prevents asking a pension or statistical body for an insurance or tax figure that does not fall within its role. In the budget of a resident, costo della vita in Svizzera is therefore read by category: the building insurance policy follows cantonal rules, LAMal follows cantonal premiums and reductions, social-security deductions follow salary, and taxation follows the three levels. The comparison is useful only if the competent body, calculation basis and applicable rule are kept separate. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. To turn the guide into a concrete check in the Canton of Bern, it is advisable to follow a short, verifiable sequence. The objective is not to estimate a premium using a generic average, but to arrive at the applicable rule, the competent authority and the correct claims procedure. ### Four operational steps 1. Define the dossier. State that the check concerns building insurance in the Canton of Bern. Keep this topic separate from LAMal/KVG, taxes and AVS/AHV or LPP/BVG contributions: they have different rules and areas of responsibility. 2. Verify the obligation. Consult the official cantonal source to determine whether, in the applicable case, the insurance is mandatory or organized differently. The same check is needed to understand which cantonal process to use. 3. Identify the provider. Establish whether the information comes from a cantonal body or an authorized insurer. At that point, coverage, premiums and the procedure to follow in the event of a claim can be considered within the same framework, without substituting data from other Cantons. 4. Handle the claim through the correct channel. When damage occurs, follow the procedure indicated by the competent authority and check the applicable deadlines and amounts with the official cantonal source. The deadlines to be met must therefore be verified through the competent channel, without importing them from other insurance policies. ### Keep the offices separate If the question concerns taxes, the institutional reference changes: AFC/ESTV for direct federal tax and VAT; cantonal administrations for cantonal and municipal taxes. If it concerns AVS, AI or LPP, UFAS/BSV operates in the field of social security and not in setting taxes. UST/BFS produces statistics, not tax rates. For each cantonal service, requirements, deadlines and amounts must be checked against the canton’s official source. This check prevents turning a figure valid for one area into an answer for another. Indexed figures, such as average LAMal premiums, change according to the year and do not replace checking the property insurance policy. To explore the social security section in greater depth, consult guida AVS/LPP e rendita. To complete the picture of disposable income, use calcolatore stipendio.

## TL;DR - Topic: cantonal elections in the Canton of Bern - Focus: calendar, voting procedures, lists and official sources - The cantonal level must be distinguished from the federal and municipal levels ## Key facts - Scope → Canton of Bern - Subject → cantonal elections - Information → electoral system, calendar, voting procedures and lists - Reference → responsible electoral office - Taxation → direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax The guide dedicated to cantonal elections covers the Canton of Bern. The editorial focus brings together the steps needed to navigate: electoral system, calendar, voting procedures, lists and the electoral office responsible for official information. The official source is therefore the starting point for checking the elements of the consultation, without automatically carrying over guidance relating to another canton or another institutional level. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the distinction matters because taxes, social security, employment, housing and the cost of living do not all fall under the same office. A guide to cantonal voting must therefore distinguish between the federal, cantonal and municipal levels. The calendar and lists relate to the consultation; the authority responsible for a tax or a benefit may instead be different. ### The map of responsibilities The tax system offers the clearest separation. In Switzerland there are three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and its own multiplier; at the municipal level, the multiplier is applied to the cantonal tax. AFC/ESTV oversees direct federal tax and VAT. The cantonal administrations, on the other hand, are responsible for cantonal and municipal taxes. For those preparing the dichiarazione delle imposte, distinguishing these three levels is more useful than reading a single tax rate out of context. Institutions also have different areas of responsibility. UFAS/BSV deals with social security, including AVS/AI/LPP, but does not set taxes. UST/BFS produces statistics and does not set tax rates. The guide to cantonal voting can be used as a map for locating the correct institutional level: for the calendar, voting procedures, lists and details of the consultation, the responsible electoral office is the reference to follow. | Scope | Reference | |---|---| | Direct federal tax and VAT | AFC/ESTV | | Cantonal and municipal taxes | cantonal administrations | | Social security | UFAS/BSV | | Statistics | UST/BFS | This grid helps clarify the practical meaning of the cantonal level without confusing it with federal or municipal responsibilities. ## Practical reading for residents and workers The practical value of the distinction emerges in everyday expenses: not all items affecting the budget, work or housing fall under the same level of responsibility. A useful reading of the cantonal vote distinguishes matters administered by the cantons and municipalities from federal rules. ### Health, services and cost of living LAMal/KVG is compulsory for residents and must be taken out within three months of arrival. It is private insurance with per-capita premiums: it is neither a tax nor a salary contribution. For adults, the deductibles are CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500. Premiums depend on the canton and region, while premium reductions are a cantonal subsidy. For the cost of living, it is therefore advisable to separate the premium, deductible and cassa malati from the tax calculation. Social assistance is generally administered by cantons and municipalities according to need. Motor vehicle taxes, energy incentives, building permits and contributions to continuing education follow cantonal rules and offices. Requirements, deadlines and amounts must be verified using the canton’s official source. The operational point here is to contact the right office, not to transfer a figure from another territory. Building insurance is compulsory or organized differently depending on the canton. Civil protection is coordinated at cantonal level within the framework of federal law; call-ups and allowances should be verified with the competent authority. Tenancy law, however, has a common federal basis: CO art. 253 et seq. is the same in every canton. The security deposit may not exceed three months’ rent and must be paid into a blocked account in the tenant’s name. A landlord’s termination notice is valid only on the official cantonal form; any challenge must be submitted to the conciliation authority within 30 days. ### Work and payslips The labor market also requires distinguishing between the federal and cantonal levels. There is no federal minimum wage, although some cantons have their own. The maximum working time is 45 hours per week in industry, offices and retail, or 50 in other sectors. The minimum vacation entitlement is four weeks, or five for those under 20; maternity leave lasts 14 weeks at 80% IPG and paternity leave two weeks. Notice periods are one, two or three months depending on seniority: first year, second to ninth year, and from the tenth year onward. On a payslip, AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG therefore remain pension-related items to be read separately from the cantonal tax level. The LPP rates on the coordinated salary are 7% between ages 25 and 34, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54, and 18% from age 55 until the reference age. For more information on AVS and LPP, consult AVS e LPP. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Practical procedure for using the guide The safest procedure starts from the official source and proceeds by levels, not by assumptions. The Canton of Bern is the geographical point of consultation; the competences listed in the guide refer instead to different offices depending on the subject matter. ### Four operational steps 1. Open the communication from the responsible electoral office. Look in the same reference for the electoral system, the calendar, the voting method, and the lists. If a detail does not appear in the official material, do not fill it in with a date or a list from another canton. 2. Classify the question before looking for the answer. For direct federal tax and VAT, the reference is FTA/ESTV; for cantonal and municipal taxes, the cantonal administrations are competent. OASI, IV, and occupational pension plans fall under social security handled by FSIO/BSV, while FSO/BFS deals with statistics. 3. Note the deadlines concerning your personal situation. Those arriving in Switzerland must take out KVG/LAMal health insurance within three months. In rental matters, the dispute must be submitted within 30 days to the conciliation authority; the deposit remains limited to three months and the landlord's termination requires the official cantonal form. For employment, the notice periods are one, two, or three months depending on the seniority indicated by the source. 4. Check the year before using an amount. Updated every year are the Pillar 3a maximum limit, the occupational pension threshold and coordination deduction, the ALV/AC maximum limit, the average KVG/LAMal premiums, and the median salary. If the year is not certain, avoid precise figures and check the official source of the canton or competent authority. To compare the impact on your budget, you can consult the cost of living in Switzerland. After checking the calendar and jurisdictions, translate the social security and salary items into your net income with the salary calculator.

item.description: Crude oil exports from the Middle East, excluding Iran, exceed pre-war levels. Brent at 101,44 dollars and WTI at 90,02: alternative routes are growing.
item.content:encoded:
In brief - Middle Eastern exports above pre-conflict average of 18 million b/d - Hormuz: previously a fifth of global hydrocarbons passed through - December Brent at $101.44; November WTI at $90.02 - Saudi Arabia and UAE have alternative pipelines
Key facts - Data source → Kpler - Pre-conflict average → 18 million barrels per day - Strategic passage → Strait of Hormuz - Saudi alternative → East-West pipeline to Yanbu - UAE alternative → pipeline to Fujairah - Brent, December delivery → $101.44, -0.79% - WTI, November delivery → $90.02, -1.20% - Quote time → Monday at 5:10 AM, Swiss time
Last week, crude exports from Middle Eastern countries, excluding Iran, surpassed the pre-war level in the region. This is indicated by data from Kpler, a maritime monitoring company. For several consecutive days, the weekly average of shipments exceeded 18 million barrels per day, the average recorded before the conflict.
The figure comes after the launch, in late February, of raids by the United States and Israel against the Islamic Republic. The count also includes flows passing through the Red Sea, a route used to circumvent the blockade that Iran is attempting to impose on the Strait of Hormuz. Before the war, a fifth of the world's consumed hydrocarbons transited through Hormuz.

## TL;DR - The maximum amounts for pillar 3a will change from January 1, 2027 - With 2nd pillar: 7373 francs, today 7258 - Without 2nd pillar: 36864 francs, today 36288 - Communication published in Bern on October 5, 2026 ## Key facts - Scope → tied individual pension provision, pillar 3a - Publication → October 5, 2026 - Location → Bern - With 2nd pillar → 7373 francs, currently 7258 - Without 2nd pillar → 36864 francs, currently 36288 - Entry into force → January 1, 2027 On October 5, 2026, in Bern, an external communication on the new limits for the maximum permitted tax deduction for tied individual pension provision, that is, pillar 3a, was published. The update concerns the 2027 tax year and distinguishes two categories based on whether a 2nd pillar is present. For people who have a 2nd pillar, the limit will rise to 7373 francs. The communication states that the current value for the same category is 7258 francs. The change therefore concerns the maximum ceiling of the permitted deduction, not a single amount valid for everyone. For people who do not have a 2nd pillar, the new limit will instead be 36864 francs, compared with the 36288 francs currently indicated. Here too, the figure is presented as the maximum tax deduction within pillar 3a. The two adjustments will enter into force on January 1, 2027. This date separates the current values reported in the communication from the new maximum amounts planned for 2027. ### Two thresholds defined by pension provision The distinction to apply is simple: anyone with a 2nd pillar falls under the first maximum; anyone without one falls under the second. The text does not present any other categories, intermediate thresholds or additional amounts. For this reason, the presence of a 2nd pillar is the first element to check when reading the update. The publication does not provide rates, estimates of savings or simulations linked to individual incomes. The text focuses on the two amounts and the effective date. The certain fact is the change to the maximum limit and its entry into force on January 1, 2027. Anyone following the topic of terzo pilastro 3a therefore finds two figures to keep distinct: the maximum amount provided for those with a 2nd pillar and the one provided for those without one. The reference remains tied individual pension provision, not a different tax item. The news focuses exclusively on tied individual pension provision. For the rest, the communication consulted adds no details on deadlines, personal calculations or different methods of application. The central points therefore remain the date of January 1, 2027, and correctly identifying one's category. ## The comparison with the Swiss tax system The change in the maximum limits does not automatically produce the same tax effect for every person. The announcement provides two certain variables: the presence of a 2nd pillar and the limit applicable from January 1, 2027. It does not provide income, tax rates or final results, so it does not allow the maximum amount to be converted into an individual figure for tax saved. ### Three levels to keep separate The pillar 3a deduction must be viewed within the Swiss tax system, which comprises direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each Canton has its own law and its own multiplier; for municipalities, the multiplier is applied to cantonal tax. The practical consequence is that the same maximum limit is not, on its own, enough to estimate the tax effect for someone living in a given area. | Situation | Current amount | From January 1, 2027 | |---|---:|---:| | With 2nd pillar | 7258 francs | 7373 francs | | Without 2nd pillar | 36288 francs | 36864 francs | The 2nd pillar referred to in the announcement is occupational pension provision LPP/BVG. Pillar 3a should not be confused with AVS/AHV: they are different elements of Swiss pension provision, while the announcement concerns exclusively the maximum deduction for 3a. The measure does not change VAT: it is a tax limit linked to pillar 3a. In a household budget, the change should be distinguished from the cost of living. It does not describe prices or wages, but the ceiling of the permitted deduction. For this reason too, the correct comparison is not between the new maximum limit and a monthly expense: it is between the threshold applicable to one's category and the previous limit. To make a personal comparison, the correct step is to enter the maximum limit in dichiarazione delle imposte and consider the applicable tax levels separately. Without income and individual tax data, the source does not allow a simulation of the final amount. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## How to apply the limit in 2027 The review can be organized without introducing figures not stated by the source. The starting point is the effective date: the new maximum amounts apply from January 1, 2027. For comparison with the previous situation, the communication reports the current limits as 7258 francs for those with a 2nd pillar and 36288 francs for those without one. ### Four-step procedure 1. Identify the year. If you are working on the 2027 tax year, consider the January 1, 2027 effective date indicated in the communication. 2. Verify the category. Ask yourself whether you have a 2nd pillar: this is the distinction used to choose the maximum amount. 3. Match the limit. With a 2nd pillar, the 2027 reference is 7373 francs; without a 2nd pillar, the reference is 36864 francs. 4. Check the tax return. Consider the maximum amount for pillar 3a in dichiarazione delle imposte without confusing the amount for your category with the other limit. This sequence avoids the most immediate error: applying 36864 francs to someone who falls into the category with a 2nd pillar, or using 7373 francs when the 2nd pillar is not present. The source does not introduce any other classifications, so it is not correct to derive a third threshold based on income, canton or other conditions not indicated. The communication does not report a deadline for submitting the tax return, an applicable tax rate or a calculation of the savings. These data cannot be added based solely on the maximum amounts. The comparison between 2026 and 2027 must also be made while keeping the current figures separate from those that will take effect on January 1, 2027.
