item.title: Lugano: the UDC proposes greater transparency regarding compensation
item.description: A motion by the UDC calls for the annual publication of the salaries of CEOs and boards of directors of companies owned by the City of Lugano.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - UDC: remuneration at companies in which Lugano holds stakes published every year - Board members and CEO identified by name - Other members of Executive Management: aggregate amount - Implementation through articles of association or shareholders' meetings ## Key facts - Promoter → UDC motion, first signatory Alain Bühler - Scope → companies in which the City of Lugano holds stakes - Board of Directors → total remuneration by name - CEO → total annual salary by name - Other executives → total aggregate amount - Publication → management report, annual report or holdings report - Criteria → uniform and comparable over time - Implementation → articles of association or proposal to other shareholders according to Lugano's shareholding ### The proposal in the Municipal Council In Lugano, a motion by the UDC, with Alain Bühler as first signatory, calls for the remuneration of the top executives of companies in which the City holds stakes to be made public every year. The request concerns members of the Boards of Directors and the highest-ranking operational officer, with the individual amounts received specified. The motion clarifies that the aim is not to determine how much the top executives should earn or to interfere in management. Instead, the UDC proposes a general transparency standard for companies in which Lugano invests public capital and exercises its shareholder rights. According to the signatories, the legal form of a joint-stock company ensures management autonomy; the presence of public capital nevertheless entails a «particular responsibility» toward the community. The model distinguishes between the Board of Directors and Executive Management. For each Board member, publication should be by name and concern total remuneration, with the main components and any compensation for chairmanships, committees or other corporate positions. For the CEO, general manager or highest-ranking operational officer, the total annual salary should be indicated by name. The other members of Executive Management would instead be reported through a single aggregate total. The intended location is a freely accessible official document: management report, annual report, holdings report or another equivalent document. The criteria should remain uniform and comparable over time, including, whenever possible, a comparison with the previous financial year. The request concerns only what the companies pay for the functions performed. Private income, assets, tax situation and other personal information are excluded. For the signatories, regular publication would serve to replace comparisons based on rumours, fragmented information, partial reconstructions or speculation with institutional data. The UDC would like to extend the principle to all of the City's corporate holdings, taking into account Lugano's shareholding. Where the City fully controls the company or has the necessary stake to amend the articles of association, the Municipal Executive should immediately take steps to include the publication requirement. Where the votes are insufficient, it should propose the same rule to the other shareholders and support it at general meetings. Finally, the motion asks the Municipal Council to approve the proposal and instruct the Municipal Executive to follow it through. ### What would change in how compensation is read If the Municipal Council were to accept the motion, the expected effect would be primarily informational: the public would be able to examine in a more orderly way how much companies with public holdings pay their top executives. It would not, however, be a decision on the level of remuneration. The proposal seeks to make the data visible, not to set an amount or take over the companies' operational management. The model creates three distinct levels of analysis. For members of the Board of Directors, the data would be linked to the individual and accompanied by the main components and any allowances. For the CEO, general manager or highest-ranking operational executive, the focus would be on the total annual salary. For the other members of General Management, the reader would instead find an aggregated total, without the same breakdown by name. The second practical element is the corporate process required to apply the rule. When Lugano's shareholding independently allows the articles of association to be amended, transparency can be included directly at that stage. When the City's votes are insufficient, the proposal must go through discussions with the other shareholders and receive support at general meetings. The motion therefore does not describe a single procedure valid for all holdings: the path depends on the City's position in the individual company. The request for uniform criteria is intended to make the data understandable over time. Comparison with the previous financial year, where possible, would make it possible to observe the evolution of remuneration without relying on partial reconstructions. That comparison, however, would not by itself establish whether compensation is appropriate: the signatories specify that the motion does not seek to determine what the level of remuneration should be. There is also a clear boundary between corporate transparency and the private sphere. The document should concern only amounts paid for the functions performed, without becoming an overview of private income, assets or tax situation. Anyone wishing to keep these two levels separate can consult busta paga svizzera for their individual remuneration; the proposal, instead, concerns the data published by the companies. Finally, the signatories refer to the experience of other Swiss cities in Public Corporate Governance and argue that a statutory rule is compatible with the entrepreneurial autonomy of public limited companies. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ### The planned course of action The motion sets out a process structured according to the City's shareholding stake. If the City Council accepts the proposal, the Municipal Council should follow it up in four steps: 1. Initiate the process requested by the City Council to apply the principle to all of the City's corporate shareholdings. 2. Verify, for each company, whether Lugano has full control or the necessary stake to amend the articles of association. 3. Include the publication obligation in the articles of association and promptly initiate the necessary steps when the amendment can be made autonomously. 4. Propose the same rule to the other shareholders and support it at general meetings when the City's votes are not enough. Once publication is required, the document to consult each year could be the management report, the annual report, the shareholdings report or another freely accessible official document. The practical check consists of verifying that the selected criterion remains consistent and that, where possible, a comparison with the previous financial year is also available. The figures should then be examined by distinguishing the different levels. The compensation of an individual board member should include the total and the main components, including any allowances for chairmanships, committees or other corporate offices. For the top operational manager, the total annual salary disclosed by name should be sought. For the other members of Executive Management, the aggregated figure should instead be considered. The scope does not include private income, assets or tax status. Including the rule in the articles of association would also serve a preventive function: according to the signatories, anyone accepting an appointment would know the publication obligations from the outset. For one's personal situation, separate from the shareholdings report, it is possible to consult the dichiarazione delle imposte. For a separate comparison of employment income, use the calcolatore stipendio. *Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/ticino/politica/1954774/compensi-di-cda-e-ceo-delle-partecipate-l-udc-vuole-piu-trasparenza)*

item.title: VAT increase for the 13th AVS pension
item.description: On 29 November, voters will decide on increasing VAT from 8,1% to 8,5% to finance the 13th AVS pension, which requires 4,2 billion francs annually.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - On November 29, the people and the Cantons will vote on the VAT increase - The standard rate would rise from 8.1% to 8.5% - The 13th AVS pension requires 4.2 billion francs - Payment is scheduled for early December
## Key facts - Popular vote → November 29 - Financing requirement → 4.2 billion francs - Annual revenue from the increase → 1.5 billion francs - Current standard VAT rate → 8.1% - Rate for the hotel sector → 4% - Reduced rate unchanged → 2.6%
On November 29, the people and the Cantons will vote on the VAT increase necessary to finance the 13th AVS pension. A 'yes' from both is essential for the project to pass.
The planned increase is 0.4 percentage points on the standard rate: from the current 8.1% to 8.5%. The goal is to avoid an excessive burden on the AVS coffers, while the payment of the additional pension is scheduled for early December.
To finance the benefit, requested by a popular initiative approved at the polls in 2024, 4.2 billion francs are needed. The requirement is expected to rise to approximately 4.5 billion in 2030 and 5.4 billion in 2040. The VAT increase would generate 1.5 billion francs per year.
### The Government's position According to Keystone-ATS, Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider presented the campaign to the media. She argued that a rejection on November 29 would have serious consequences and that, without additional flows, the AVS would find itself in an increasingly precarious financial situation.
> «a 'no' on November 29 would have serious consequences»
The Federal Councillor defined the 'yes' at the polls as important and indicated the proposal resulting from parliamentary deliberations as a socially sustainable compromise. The Government and the Chambers consider it balanced because all generations would contribute to guaranteeing the 13th AVS and a certain balance of accounts.
The compromise provides for a moderate increase in the standard rate and the transition of the rate for the hotel sector from 3.8% to 4%. The reduced rate remains at 2.6% for daily goods, including food and medicines. According to Baume-Schneider, this approach would lighten the burden on economically weaker individuals and families.
A minority in Parliament and the FDP oppose the proposal. The former fears a weakening of purchasing power and points to structural measures, such as an increase in the retirement age, currently set at 65 for everyone. The FDP, on the other hand, believes that the increase would weigh heavily on families and SMEs. To follow the topic of the pension, the AVS guide is available. ## Two scenarios for the AVS accounts
The Confederation's estimates reveal a concrete difference between the two outcomes of the consultation. If the ballot boxes were to reject the financing, the annual deficits of the first pillar would rise to almost 5 billion by 2035. With the VAT increase, the same figure could be reduced to around 3 billion.
| Outcome | Annual deficit in 2035 | AVS fund in 2035 | |---|---|---| | Rejection at the ballot box | almost 5 billion francs | around 50% | | VAT increase | around 3 billion francs | around 70% |
The AVS fund adds a second indicator. As early as 2027, it risks falling below the threshold provided for by law of 100% of annual expenditure. In 2035, according to the estimates cited, the level would be around 50% without the increase and 70% with the new revenue. The comparison therefore concerns both the current deficit and the fund's assets.
### Rates and purchasing power From the perspective of households, the proposal does not modify all rates in the same way. The standard rate would rise from 8,1% to 8,5%, the rate for the hotel sector would increase from 3,8 to 4%, while the reduced rate would remain at 2,6% for everyday goods, including food and medicines.
This distinction supports Baume-Schneider's argument that the solution is socially sustainable. The opposing view is that of the parliamentary minority and the FDP: a higher VAT would weaken purchasing power, burdening households and SMEs. The cost of living thus enters the debate through the differing assessment of the levy and the structural alternatives.
The proposal compares an increase in revenue with the possibility of intervening on the retirement age, currently set at 65 for everyone. To explore the impact on the household budget in greater depth, see costo della vita in Svizzera.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## How to orient yourself before the vote
For those who live or work in Switzerland, a practical assessment of the proposal can follow four checks, all linked to the data cited in the campaign.
### Three practical checks 1. Note the date and the parties involved. On November 29, the decision lies with the people and the Cantons: the proposal requires approval from both components.
2. **Separate the rates.** The planned increase is 0,4 percentage points, from 8,1% to 8,5% for the standard rate. The rate for the hospitality sector would rise from 3,8 to 4%, while the reduced rate would remain at 2,6% for everyday goods, food and medicines.
3. Set out the amounts. Financing requires 4,2 billion francs; the need is expected to reach 4,5 billion in 2030 and 5,4 billion in 2040. New revenue is estimated at 1,5 billion a year.
4. Compare the positions. The Government and the Chambers describe the solution as balanced and socially sustainable. The parliamentary minority and PLR, however, point to purchasing power, the burden on families and SMEs, and the possibility of structural measures.
Payment of the 13th pension is scheduled for early December. This date should be kept distinct from the November 29 vote: the former concerns the payment indicated in the source, the latter the funding needed to support it.
To follow pension-related matters, you can consult guida alla rendita AVS. To assess your own financial leeway, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Parmelin in India: agreement to protect investments
item.description: From New Delhi, Guy Parmelin reports that Bern hopes for an agreement on investment protection and highlights the importance of intellectual property.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Guy Parmelin arrived in New Delhi for three days - Bern wants to conclude the investment agreement soon - The India-EFTA agreement has been in force for a year - Mobility, training and science are included in the declaration of intent ## Key facts - Protagonist → Guy Parmelin - Location → New Delhi - Duration → three-day state visit - Counterpart → Prime Minister Narendra Modi - Objective → rapid conclusion of the agreement on investment protection - Related dossier → intellectual property - Trade agreement → India and the EFTA countries - Declaration of intent → migration and mobility Guy Parmelin arrived in New Delhi for a three-day state visit, with the economic dossier at the centre of the talks. After talks with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Swiss economics minister said that Bern hoped for the rapid conclusion of an agreement on investment protection. The stated objective is to further stimulate investment. ### The three elements of the visit The Vaud native linked this step to the results of the discussions on intellectual property, which he attaches great importance to. The trade agreement between India and the EFTA countries was presented as beneficial to both sides. The framework emerging from the visit comprises three distinct elements. The first is the trade and economic agreement between India and the EFTA countries, which entered into force a year ago after 16 years of negotiations. The function identified by Bern is to improve Swiss companies' access to the Indian market and increase legal certainty. The second is the agreement on investment protection. Switzerland hopes for its rapid conclusion: the source therefore presents it as an objective still being pursued, not as an agreement that has already been concluded. The third is the declaration of intent that Bern and New Delhi agreed on migration and mobility, with a specific focus on training and scientific cooperation. For Switzerland, the mission therefore brings together trade, investment, intellectual property and mobility. The source gives no date for the conclusion of the investment agreement or operational details for the declaration of intent. The central point remains the call to accelerate investment protection, while the trade agreement already in force constitutes the reference indicated for market access. The sequence described by New Delhi therefore distinguishes an already operational result from two tracks still to be developed. For the first agreement, the source speaks of business access and legal certainty; for the second, of rapid conclusion; for the declaration of intent, of training and scientific cooperation. These, and no other details, are the results attributed to the visit. ## What it means for the Swiss economy For a Swiss company interested in India, the news should be read as a sequence of dossiers with different statuses. There is not a single announcement: the trade and economic agreement has already been in force for a year, investment protection is the objective Bern wants to conclude quickly, while intellectual property and mobility complete the political and economic discussions. ### Status of the dossiers | Dossier | Status indicated | Impact described | | --- | --- | --- | | Trade and economic agreement | In force for a year, after 16 years of negotiations | Improve Swiss companies' access to the Indian market and legal certainty | | Investment protection | Switzerland hopes for a swift conclusion | Further stimulate investment | | Intellectual property | Results of the discussions considered important | Element linked to the investment dossier | | Migration and mobility | Declaration of intent agreed | Training and scientific cooperation | The distinction is useful because it prevents confusing a trade agreement that has already entered into force with an investment agreement that is still pending. For a Swiss company, the first point of reference indicated by the source is access to the Indian market; the second is the prospect of greater investment protection, but the source does not say that the new agreement has already been signed or implemented. Intellectual property should also be considered an open dossier in the discussions. Parmelin emphasized the significance of the negotiation results, without providing further details. Consequently, the news does not make it possible to quantify effects or timelines for an individual company. ### The mobility section The declaration of intent concerns migration and mobility, but the source identifies only two areas: training and scientific cooperation. No individual procedures are described for anyone intending to move between Switzerland and India. The concrete fact is therefore the opening of a channel of cooperation, not the announcement of a new personal pathway. For the Swiss reader, the news offers a practical key: distinguish what is already operational from what Bern hopes to conclude. To follow the national employment aspect without attributing to it effects the source does not describe, one can consult the aziende che assumono. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to read and use the news To read the mission without confusing the instruments, one can proceed in four steps, staying within the information communicated by Bern and New Delhi. 1. Separate trade from investment. The India-EFTA trade and economic agreement is the one that entered into force a year ago, after 16 years of negotiations. Investment protection is instead the agreement that Switzerland hopes to conclude quickly. They should not be presented as the same agreement. 2. Identify the stated effect. For the trade agreement, the source indicates two objectives: improving Swiss companies' access to the Indian market and increasing legal certainty. For the future investment agreement, the intended effect is to further stimulate investment. 3. Keep intellectual property separate. Parmelin attaches great importance to the results of the discussions on this dossier. Until the source reports a more detailed outcome, the correct wording is to speak of results considered important, without turning it into a rule that has already been defined. 4. Read the statement on mobility for what it says. Bern and New Delhi have agreed on a declaration of intent on migration and mobility, with reference to training and scientific cooperation. The text does not present it as a new individual pathway that can already be activated. ### A practical guide for companies and readers An internal guide can therefore state the name of the dossier, its status and the stated objective. For trade: agreement in force, market access and legal certainty. For investment: rapid conclusion hoped for and investment stimulus. For mobility and training: declaration of intent and scientific cooperation. This grid avoids attributing to the visit measures that the source does not announce. The same caution is needed by those looking for personal consequences in Switzerland. The text talks about companies, investment, intellectual property, training and scientific cooperation; it does not describe individual changes linked to everyday life. For a separate banking topic, the portal gathers information on conti bancari in Svizzera; for the labor market, aziende che assumono are available. These tools do not replace the details of the agreement, which will have to be clarified in subsequent steps. To assess your personal income situation instead, use calcolatore stipendio e imposte. *Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/guy-parmelin-in-india%3a-per-un-accordo-che-protegga-gli-investimenti/92167943)*

item.title: Cyber risks: Swiss SMEs underestimate the dangers
item.description: A VZ-HSLU analysis indicates that cyber incidents are the top global risk: nearly 58'000 digital crimes in Switzerland in 2025.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - SMEs still underestimate cyber risks - Allianz ranks them first globally in 2026 - Nearly 58'000 digital crimes in Switzerland in 2025 - Just under 12% of companies have coverage ## Key facts - Study → VermögensZentrum and HSLU - Risk Barometer 2026 → cyber incidents in first place - Global costs in 2024 → approximately 9,5 trillion US dollars - Digital crimes in Switzerland in 2025 → nearly 58'000 - Resolution rate → 17,6% - Coverage in Switzerland → just under 12% ### The danger does not remain in the IT department Nearly 58'000 crimes committed using digital means were recorded in Switzerland in 2025. The crime statistics cited by VZ add a high number of unreported cases, while the resolution rate stood at 17,6%. This is the Swiss picture highlighted by the study published today by VermögensZentrum in collaboration with Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts, HSLU. The research starts from a belief still held by many small and medium-sized enterprises: that they are not affected by cyber threats. For VZ and HSLU, this assumption is dangerous. The reason given is that the consequences go beyond the IT sphere. An attack can disrupt operations, damage data and systems, jeopardize customer relationships, trigger legal obligations or put a company's liquidity under severe strain. In the worst-case scenario, the very existence of the SME is at stake. VZ points to Allianz's Risk Barometer 2026, which for the fifth consecutive time ranked cyber incidents first among business risks globally. Estimates of the costs caused by cybercrime worldwide in 2024 reach approximately 9,5 trillion US dollars. If it were a national economy, cybercrime would be the world's third-largest, after the United States and China. ### From perception to management VZ and HSLU wanted to understand how SMEs can properly understand, classify and insure against cyber risks as part of effective management. The study starts from a precise limitation: cyber threats cannot be avoided entirely. Management therefore requires greater knowledge of digital dependencies, clarified responsibilities, emergency procedures and a conscious assessment of the financial consequences. This approach links cyber risk to the overall management of the company, not to a single department. ## Risk should be understood as a business issue The most useful piece of information for an SME, in the reading proposed by VZ and HSLU, is not merely the existence of a cyber threat. It is the way in which an attack can shift the problem from a single system to the entire business. The source encourages understanding and classifying risks precisely because the consequences can affect operations, data, customers, legal obligations and liquidity. ### A map of the consequences | Affected element | Effect indicated by the source | |---|---| | Operations | Disruption | | Data and systems | Damage | | Customer relationships | Compromise | | Legal obligations | Possible activation | | Liquidity | Pressure | This map helps avoid two opposite mistakes. The first is to treat the incident as an issue confined to IT, ignoring the financial side and customer relationships. The second is to rely solely on the policy, even though the study considers insurance a fundamental component. Coverage, however, does not replace prevention or effective hazard management. For those managing an SME, the question is not whether the risk can be eliminated: the study says that cyber threats cannot be avoided entirely. The question becomes which digital dependencies the company knows about, which responsibilities have been clarified and which emergency procedures have been prepared. At that point, the assessment must reach the financial consequences. The Swiss figure on coverage remains the one indicated by the study: just under 12% of companies have coverage. The percentage should be read together with the other indication from VZ and HSLU: insurance is a fundamental component, but it does not replace prevention and effective management. For a separate reference on personal expenses, costo della vita in Svizzera is available. The internal review can start with the effect and work back to the dependency that generates it. If operations are interrupted, the consequence for business functioning is examined; if data and systems are damaged, what is involved is clarified; if customers are affected, the relationship is considered; if legal obligations or pressure on liquidity emerge, the assessment moves beyond purely technical language. This is the distinction between technology and management that the study asks SMEs to make. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## A five-step internal procedure The study does not propose eliminating risk, but indicates how to manage it better. The guidance can become a concrete workflow for an SME. 1. Map digital dependencies. Start with the systems and data on which the business depends. Knowledge of these dependencies is the starting point the study identifies for better risk management. 2. Clarify responsibilities. Define who handles the various steps in managing cyber risks, so that the issue has an internal point of reference. 3. Prepare emergency procedures. Organize the response to business interruption and damage to data and systems described in the research. 4. Assess the financial consequences. Consciously consider liquidity, customer relationships and any legal obligations that may result from an attack. 5. Examine insurance. Coverage against cyber risks is a fundamental component, but it must be accompanied by prevention and effective risk management. ### A choice that does not replace prevention The fifth step does not mean shifting all responsibility to the policy. According to VZ and HSLU, insurance replaces neither prevention nor effective management. The Swiss figure, with just under 12% of companies having coverage, indicates that insurance protection should be considered within overall management and not in isolation. The process also serves to distinguish technical severity from business impact. A damaged system or piece of data can be assessed based on its effect on the business; a compromise of customer relationships must be considered together with legal obligations; pressure on liquidity forms part of the financial assessment. These are the effects described by the source, rearranged into an operational sequence. For the banking aspect of liquidity management, consult conti bancari in Svizzera. To complement the business analysis with a review of personal finances, use calcolatore stipendio/imposte. *Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/rischi-informatici-sottovalutati-da-molte-pmi%2c-studio/92167766)*

## TL;DR - login Ticino Open Doors: Saturday, October 10, 09.00-13.00 - Railway, technical and digital professions are explored in Bellinzona - Visits to the FFS Workshops, including areas not open to the public - New Federal VET Diploma training for buildings and infrastructure from August 2027 ## Key facts - Event → login Ticino Open Doors - Location → Bellinzona - Time → Saturday, October 10, from 09.00 to 13.00 - New feature → Building and Infrastructure IT Specialist Federal VET Diploma - Start → August 2027 - Duration → four years - First year → entirely at school - After the first year → alternating between school and professional practice ### A journey between railways and digital technology On Saturday, October 10, from 09.00 to 13.00, Bellinzona will be the meeting point for the login Ticino Open Doors. The event is aimed at girls, boys and families interested in getting a close look at vocational training and activities related to transport, technology and infrastructure. Those interested in working on tracks can observe a profession related to the safety and efficiency of the Swiss railway network. Those looking at building technology can focus on the integration of networks, security, access, video surveillance, automation, and energy management. Those who want to understand customer relations will find the training for Retail Specialist EFZ in the login Pavilion. The new digital training also features a particular structure. The first year is entirely at school, allowing for the acquisition of solid technical foundations before entering the corporate world, as indicated by the presentation. The following three years alternate between school-based training and professional practice. For a family needing guidance, this element allows them to evaluate not only the technical content of the profile but also how study and professional activity are distributed over time. The day also relates railway maintenance to the digitalization of public infrastructure, transport, and intelligent buildings. These are areas described by the source as rich in prospects and linked to concrete skills. After identifying the direction closest to your interests, you can broaden your search by consulting companies that are hiring, without confusing initial orientation with a definitive choice. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to prepare your visit ### Five useful steps 1. Mark Saturday, October 10th, from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM on your calendar. The reference point is Bellinzona, where the login Ticino Open Doors event takes place. Bringing the schedule with you will help you make the most of the various opportunities offered during the morning. 2. Decide which career path to explore first. In the login Pavilion, you can start with the training for Retail Specialist EFZ. Outdoors, you can observe the activities of Track Construction Workers EFZ. The goal is to arrive at the visit with a concrete question about daily work. 3. During the demonstrations, note down the tools, techniques, and materials that capture your attention the most. Meeting apprentices and professionals will allow you to connect the observed activities with the skills required for different professions, going beyond a simple description of the training title. 4. Include guided tours of the SBB Workshops in your itinerary. Access to areas normally not open to the public will allow you to observe the maintenance of modern electric trains and industrial painting, as well as the technologies, processes, and skills related to rolling stock. 5. Dedicate part of your visit to the preview scheduled for August 2027. For the four-year training program for Building and Infrastructure Informatics Specialist EFZ, gather information about the first year entirely at school and the subsequent three years of alternating between school-based training and professional practice. The assessment can focus on IT networks, safety systems, access control, video surveillance, building automation, energy management, and smart building technologies. This type of preparation transforms the morning into an orientation journey. Young people and families can leave the visit with a comparison of railway, technical, digital, and retail activities, connecting their interests and talents to the professions presented. Those who wish to continue their evaluation can consult the job postings and, for an initial income orientation, use the salary calculator. *Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/rubriche/aziende-ticinesi-informano/1954740/edifici-formazione-vicino-futuro-infrastrutture-afc-binari)*

item.title: Villa Principe Leopoldo closes for renovations and lays off staff
item.description: The Hotel Villa Principe Leopoldo in Collina d'Oro will close from December 30 for 12 million in renovation work. 76 layoffs out of 81 employees are expected, with reopening in May.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 76 layoffs out of 81 employees - Last day of service: December 30 - Reopening scheduled for May - Investment in the work: 12 million francs ## Key facts - Property → Hotel Villa Principe Leopoldo - Company → Dot Life SA - Location → Collina d'Oro - Staff → 76 layoffs out of 81 employees - Investment → 12 million francs for the work December 30 will be the last day of service for the Hotel Villa Principe Leopoldo in Collina d'Oro, a luxury property in the Lugano area. The closure will be temporary: after several months of work, reopening is scheduled for May and completion of the work is set for May 1st. ### Communication to staff The plan was communicated by Dot Life SA in a letter signed by the CEO and the President of the Board of Directors and sent to employees. The company plans to invest 12 million francs to bring the property up to contemporary standards. The closure had already been discussed in mid-September, and its consequences for staff had been confirmed. The plan calls for collective layoffs among staff. There would be 76 layoffs among the 81 people currently employed. Some department heads, however, are expected to remain employed to carry out duties related to preparing for the reopening and supporting the work. The actual layoffs are ideally expected to be announced between October and November 2026. For most employees, the last working day will be December 30, while December 31 will be a paid day off. The company also plans support measures and a loyalty bonus for those who continue working until the last day stipulated in their contract. > «We are fully aware of the impact this scenario may have on each of you, both personally and professionally.» Dot Life describes the measure as temporary and says it intends to rehire the employees needed to resume operations. However, the same letter specifies that it is not possible to guarantee that everyone will return: the factors listed include possible delays in the work, a gradual reopening and possible scaling back related to the project. The modernization of Principe Leopoldo is part of a broader program concerning Dot Life SA's properties, which also includes Villa Sassa. The total investment is approximately 52 million francs, of which 40 million, the larger share, are earmarked for Villa Sassa. ## The critical issue is continuity of employment For those who work at the facility, the decisive factor is not only the date announced for the reopening. It is the gap between the end of employment for most of the staff and a new hire that remains subject to the project's needs. The source distinguishes between the resumption of operations and the return of each employee. ### Three scenarios to distinguish The first scenario concerns those whose contract comes to an end. In this case, the schedule indicated by the company includes the last day of work, paid leave on December 31, support measures and a loyalty bonus for those who will have worked until the scheduled expiry date. These elements concern the exit phase and do not constitute, in the letter, a promise of a return. The second scenario concerns the department heads who are expected to remain during preparations for the reopening and while the work is being carried out. Their continued presence shows that staffing needs change during the different phases: some roles are already needed during the closure phase, while others will depend on the gradual resumption of operations. The third scenario begins with the scheduled date of May 1st. Although that is the deadline indicated for the completion of the work, the company links rehiring to the number of employees needed. A delay, a gradual start or a scaling back of the project may therefore change the timing and number of people returning. The capital allocated to the work is not presented as an employment guarantee: the letter leaves open the possibility that not all current employees will be rehired. For the local area, the case offers a concrete comparison between investment and employment. Dot Life announces 12 million for Principe Leopoldo and approximately 52 million for the program involving its properties, but the staff must contend with a reorganization that comes before the reopening. The size of the investment or the indicated date alone therefore do not determine the individual outcome; what matter are the role, the duration of the work and the staffing needs in the subsequent phase. Those who need to prepare for a possible change of employment can consult annunci di lavoro. To assess the effect of a transition period on daily expenses, costo della vita in Svizzera is also available. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to navigate the transition Managing the coming months requires separating the steps already indicated by the company from the conditions still tied to the project. For staff, the useful sequence starts with the communication received and leads to checking for any roles in the reopening, without confusing the scheduled date for completion of the work with individual confirmation. ### A practical sequence 1. Keep the letter sent by the company and check which date applies to your position. For most people, the reference is December 30 as the last day of work; December 31 is indicated as paid leave. 2. Mark the period between October and November 2026, when the actual layoffs should ideally be communicated. This is the step indicated by the company for understanding the concrete impact of the measure on staff. 3. Separate the duties involved in preparing for the reopening and supporting the works from the positions necessary for resuming operations. The letter indicates that some department heads should remain for the first phase. 4. Treat May 1st as the expected date for completion of the works, not as individual confirmation of a return. Dot Life states that it intends to rehire the necessary employees, but ties the decision to progress, the phased reopening and the size of the project. 5. Check the support measures and the loyalty bonus if you continue working until the last day stipulated by the contract. At the same time, those who will need to seek new employment can plan an alternative path without waiting for the outcome of the reopening. This timeline helps distinguish what has already been scheduled from what remains conditional: the closure, the last day of work and the leave are specified; returning, by contrast, depends on the roles needed. item.title: VAT vote for AHV: date and details of the federal vote
item.description: On November 26, 2026, a vote will be held on financing the AVS 13th monthly payment through the VAT increase. Discover rates, deadlines, and impacts on the budget.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The vote on VAT for the AVS is scheduled for November 26, 2026. - The 13th AVS monthly payment will be paid in December 2026. - The reduced rate would remain unchanged at 2,6%. - The Federal Council and Parliament recommend voting yes.
## Key facts - Vote → November 26, 2026 - Publication → October 5, 2026 - First payment → December 2026 - Reduced rate → 2,6% - Questions and answers → September 22, 2026
In Bern, the press release published on October 5, 2026 announces that a vote will be held on November 26, 2026, on additional financing for the AVS through an increase in VAT. The Federal Council and Parliament recommend approving an increase of 0,4 percentage points.
The measure finances part of the 13th monthly payment of the AVS old-age pension, paid for the first time in December 2026 to around 2,6 million beneficiaries. The amount can reach 2520 francs more in pension per year; for married couples, the press release indicates up to 3780 francs. The additional costs for the insurance will initially exceed 4 billion francs per year and surpass 5 billion from 2035.
### The insurance schedule and accounts
In 2026, AVS expenditure will already exceed revenue by more than 1 billion francs. Without additional revenue, the Confederation's current estimates indicate that annual deficits would reach almost 5 billion in 2035. Reserves would decline: in 2027, the AVS Fund would fall below the threshold of 100 percent of one year's expenditure set by law, while in 2035 it would risk reaching around 50 percent.
The proposal provides for an increase in the standard rate from 8,1 to 8,5 percent and in the special rate for the hotel sector from 3,8 to 4,0 percent. The reduced rate, however, would remain at 2,6 percent. This choice excludes from the increase goods identified as everyday-use items, including foodstuffs, medicines, newspapers, books, menstrual hygiene products and certain agricultural work and goods.
The VAT increase can enter into force at the earliest at the beginning of 2028, while the first payment of the 13th monthly payment is already scheduled for December 2026. A minority in Parliament believes that the increase would reduce purchasing power. It calls for the expenditure of the 13th monthly payment to be addressed in the next AVS reform and identifies an increase in the reference age among the structural measures. The published documentation also includes the questions and answers from September 22, 2026. Per seguire la rendita, consulta la guida AVS. ## The proposal from the perspective of the family budget
For a practical reading, the project should be broken down into two effects: spending subject to VAT and the financial trajectory of AVS. The increase is not uniform, because the reduced rate remains unchanged while the standard and special hotel rates change.
### Two effects to separate
| Item | Today | Proposal | |---|---:|---:| | Standard VAT | 8,1% | 8,5% | | Hotel sector | 3,8% | 4,0% | | Goods subject to the reduced rate | 2,6% | 2,6% |
For households with low to middle incomes, maintaining 2,6% is the most tangible point. The statement explains that these households devote a higher share of their spending to everyday goods than households with higher incomes. Leaving the reduced rate unchanged therefore limits the burden on the items considered most recurrent in the daily budget.
The difference between the rates makes it impossible to speak of an identical increase on every purchase. The listed goods remain at 2,6%; for items subject to the standard rate, the proposal would raise it from 8,1 to 8,5, while the hotel sector would go from 3,8 to 4,0. The financing, moreover, is presented as a distribution between workers and pension beneficiaries: through VAT, according to the Federal Council and Parliament, all generations would contribute.
### The comparison of reserves
The second effect concerns reserves. The VAT increase would provide approximately 1,5 billion francs per year to AVS. The measure would reduce the deficit forecast for 2035 from nearly 5 to approximately 3 billion francs and would raise the Fund's level from approximately 50 to approximately 70 percent of annual expenditure.
| Assumption | Annual deficit in 2035 | AVS Fund in 2035 | |---|---:|---:| | Without additional revenue | nearly 5 billion | approximately 50% of annual expenditure | | With the VAT increase | approximately 3 billion | approximately 70% of annual expenditure |
The comparison shows an improvement, not the elimination of the deficit. This is the crux of the choice: the Federal Council and Parliament see VAT as a contribution distributed across generations and as protection for reserves; the minority, on the other hand, fears the effect on purchasing power and prefers to also discuss structural measures in the next reform. To connect the discussion to a family's expenses, costo della vita in Svizzera can be used, keeping purchases subject to the reduced rate separate from the other items.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Before November 26: how to organize the review
Anyone who wants to reach November 26 with an orderly overview can prepare a personal worksheet, separating the date of the vote, the date of the first AVS payment, and the possible date when the VAT increase takes effect. These are three different points in time: the vote is on November 26, 2026, the 13th monthly payment begins in December 2026, and the increase may enter into force no earlier than the beginning of 2028.
### Four practical steps
1. Mark the political deadline. November 26, 2026, is the voting date indicated by the Confederation. On the sheet, also note that the increase is not expected before the beginning of 2028: this avoids confusing the decision with the application of the new rate.
2. Check the family's social security situation. If there is a pension beneficiary, record December 2026 as the first disbursement of the AVS 13th monthly payment and include the annual maximums indicated in the press release, distinguishing the figure indicated for beneficiaries from the one indicated for married couples. Do not turn those maximums into an identical amount for every beneficiary.
3. Gather the relevant expenses. In one column, list the everyday-use goods mentioned in the text, for which the reduced rate would remain at 2,6%. For the other items, note the standard rate and the special rate separately, using the comparison between 8,1 and 8,5 percent and between 3,8 and 4,0 percent indicated in the proposal.
4. Read the official documents before forming an opinion. The press release refers to the information sheet on VAT and the financing of social insurance: historical overview and the questions-and-answers document on the vote. The dates given are October 5, 2026, for the information sheet and September 22, 2026, for the questions and answers. Then compare the two positions: the Federal Council and Parliament focus on financial stability, while the minority points to purchasing power and structural measures.
This checklist is intended to avoid mixing support for the 13th monthly payment with the cost of VAT and to read the proposal using the available data, without adding individual estimates. To translate the comparison into your budget, use calcolatore stipendio.
*Source: [admin.ch](https://www.admin.ch/it/newnsb/gZ4zhuBYFjyi)*

item.title: Rents in Switzerland: 32% increase in twenty years
item.description: The Swiss Tenants Association reports rent increases of 32,1% between 2005 and 2025. Pressure on low and middle incomes and new political demands.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Rents have risen by 32% in 20 years - The index grew by 32,1% between 2005 and 2025 - The reference rate is 1,25% - Gross incomes of up to 4'000 francs: 37,8% goes toward rent ## Key facts - Organization → Swiss Tenants' Association (ASI) - Location → Bern - Renting in Switzerland → two thirds of households - Rent index → 32,1% between 2005 and 2025 - Reference rate → 1,25% - Gross income → up to 4'000 francs, with 37,8% allocated to rent - OECD comparison → one low-income family out of two exceeds 40% - Investment companies → 28,7% in 2000 and 44,4% in 2024 ### ASI's position Rents in Switzerland have increased by about 32% over the past 20 years, according to the Swiss Tenants' Association (ASI). In Bern, on the occasion of International Tenants' Day, the organization drew attention to the financial burden weighing on tenants and called for measures to be adopted. The scope is national: according to ASI, two thirds of households live in rented accommodation. For those who pay rent, the issue therefore enters costo della vita in Svizzera, but the association's criticism concerns above all the gap between the trend in interest rates and that of rents. Between 2005 and 2025, the rent index grew by 32,1%. During the same period, mortgage rates reached an all-time low. The reference rate currently stands at 1,25%. Since rents are legally indexed to this rate, many should have decreased. According to ASI, however, they continued to rise. The pressure particularly affects low- and middle-income households. People whose gross income does not exceed 4'000 francs allocate 37,8% of their income to rent. OECD data for eight countries, including Switzerland, also show that one in two low-income renting families allocates more than 40% of its disposable income to rent. Affordable housing is meanwhile becoming rarer. ASI's analysis also records a change in ownership of rental housing: the share belonging to private individuals fell from 57,3% in 2000 to 43,2% in 2024, while that of owner investment companies rose from 28,7% to 44,4%. According to the association, these companies achieved high returns through the real estate sector. ASI calls for a change of course, the application of the cost-based rent principle, a strengthening of the Lex Koller to curb the influx of financial capital into the residential market, and more public-interest housing. It also criticizes the indirect counterproposal envisaged by the Federal Council in response to the Rent Initiative: according to the association, it would lead to an even more marked increase in rents. ## The comparison that weighs on family budgets The shift from predominantly private ownership to a broader presence of investment companies is one of the key figures that allows us to read the market beyond the overall increase in rents. The shares indicated by the ASI are as follows: | Rental housing owners | 2000 | 2024 | |---|---:|---:| | Private individuals | 57.3% | 43.2% | | Investment companies | 28.7% | 44.4% | Between 2000 and 2024, therefore, the share of housing belonging to private individuals decreased, while that of investment companies increased. The ASI links the latter to high returns in the real estate sector. This data does not quantify the rent of each individual home, but describes a transformation of the ownership structure that the association associates with the scarcity of accessible housing. ### Two different bases for measuring the burden Pressure on families must be read by separating two metrics. The first concerns people with a gross income of up to CHF 4,000: according to the ASI, 37.8% of their income is allocated to rent. The second comes from the OECD comparison across eight countries, including Switzerland: one in two low-income tenant families spends more than 40% of their disposable income on rent. The two percentages do not describe the same audience nor the same calculation basis. The 37.8% refers to the gross income of people below the indicated threshold; the 40% concerns the disposable income of low-income families in the international comparison. Separating these indicators avoids adding them together or using them as if they were identical. To organize the comparison between gross income and disposable income, one can start from the Swiss payslip. Even the reference interest rate remains a point to verify. The source recalls that rents are legally indexed to this rate and that many, with the value at 1.25%, should have decreased. The fact that they have instead continued to grow is the crux highlighted by the ASI. Since two-thirds of households live in rented accommodation, the problem does not affect a marginal segment, but a large component of Swiss families. The combination of income burden, scarcer accessible housing, and changing ownership explains why the association is calling for political intervention. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## Four steps to understand the problem To turn the data into a personal assessment, it is useful to follow a simple sequence and keep the quantities used by the source separate. ### Income first, then rent 1. Separate the calculation bases. Record gross income and, separately, disposable income. The source uses the former as the reference for people whose income does not exceed 4'000 francs and the latter in the OECD comparison. Confusing the two values leads to an imprecise assessment of the rent burden. 2. Measure the share allocated to housing. For the gross-income bracket indicated by ASI, the reference is 37,8% of income allocated to rent. When disposable income is used, OECD data indicate that one in two low-income renter households exceeds 40%. The two thresholds serve to interpret different situations. 3. Distinguish proposals from measures already announced. ASI calls for the application of cost-based rent, strengthening Lex Koller to curb the inflow of financial capital into the residential real-estate market, and a larger number of public-interest housing units. These are the demands put forward by the association, not individual procedures described in the source. 4. Follow the federal political process. ASI criticizes the indirect counterproposal planned by the Federal Council in response to the Rent Initiative and argues that it would cause an even more pronounced increase in rents. This is the institutional point to watch when assessing the evolution of the national framework. This sequence makes it possible to link the rent burden to the correct income, distinguish the Swiss comparison from the OECD one, and identify which interventions are ASI demands. To complete the calculation of disposable income and taxes, use calcolatore stipendio/imposte. *Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/attualita/1954697/svizzera-associazione-reddito-alloggi-affitti-anni)*

item.title: Rents in Switzerland: +32% in twenty years, ASI sounds the alarm
item.description: The Swiss Tenants' Association reports a 32,1% increase between 2005 and 2025. Low incomes are under pressure: those earning less than 4'000 francs spend 37,8% on housing.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Rents increased by around 32% in twenty years - Rent index: +32,1% between 2005 and 2025 - Reference rate: 1,25% today - Incomes up to 4'000 francs: 37,8% spent on rent ## Key facts - Organization → Swiss Tenants' Association (ASI) - Occasion → International Tenants' Day - Share renting → two thirds of households - Index period → 2005-2025 - Index increase → 32,1% - Reference rate → 1,25% - Gross income considered → up to 4'000 francs - Comparative data → eight countries, including Switzerland, according to the OECD The figure, amounting to an increase in rents of around 32% over approximately twenty years, is what the ASI is using to draw attention to the burden of renting in Switzerland. The Keystone-ATS text reports that, on the occasion of International Tenants' Day, the association called on policymakers to take measures against the financial burden weighing on households. In Switzerland, two thirds of households live in rented accommodation. The source adds that in no other European country is the percentage of people living in rented accommodation so high. According to the ASI, the rent index rose by 32,1% between 2005 and 2025. During the same period, mortgage rates reached an all-time low. The reference rate is currently 1,25%. Since rents are legally indexed to this rate, many rents should have fallen; the association deplores the fact that they have continued to rise. The ASI sees this discrepancy as the central point of the warning. ### The burden on lower incomes The pressure is concentrated among households with low and medium incomes. People whose gross income does not exceed 4'000 francs spend 37,8% of their income on rent. OECD data relating to eight countries, including Switzerland, also indicate that one in two low-income renting households spends more than 40% of its disposable income on housing. The ASI also points to the shortage of affordable housing. In 2000, 57,3% of rental housing belonged to private individuals; in 2024, the share had fallen to 43,2%. Over the same period, the share owned by investment companies rose from 28,7% to 44,4%. According to the association's analysis, these companies achieved high returns through the real estate sector. The demand is for a political change of course, with the application of the principle of cost-based rents, a strengthening of the Lex Koller and a greater number of public-benefit housing units. Finally, the ASI criticizes the Federal Council's indirect counterproposal to the Rent Initiative: according to the association, it would lead to an even sharper increase in rents. ## From statistics to the household budget An average increase in the index does not have the same effect on every contract. For a family, the real burden depends on the ratio between rent and disposable income, precisely the point that emerges from the comparison between the 37,8% recorded for gross incomes up to 4'000 francs and the OECD figure: one in two low-income renter households spends more than 40% of its disposable income on rent. Housing thus becomes an expense that affects the cost of living, especially as affordable housing becomes scarcer. To assess this pressure alongside other expenses, costo della vita in Svizzera is available. ### Before and after in housing ownership | Ownership of rental housing | 2000 | 2024 | | Private owners | 57,3% | 43,2% | | Property-owning investment companies | 28,7% | 44,4% | The comparison shows a shift in the ownership structure without describing any individual building or individual contract. The share of private owners has decreased, while that of investment companies has grown. These data do not link every rent increase to a specific owner. ASI, on the other hand, states that investment companies have achieved high returns thanks to the real estate sector. The shift from one form of ownership to another does not allow the price of each apartment to be inferred. It does, however, show the change accompanying the association's demands: more transparency regarding the relationship between cost and rent, less inflow of financial capital into the residential market, and more public-interest housing. For those looking for or already occupying a home, ASI's proposals fall into three directions: applying the principle of cost-based rent, strengthening Lex Koller to curb the inflow of financial capital into the residential real estate market, and increasing public-interest housing. These are political demands, not a description of a new individual rent. The reference to the Federal Council concerns the indirect counterproposal to the Rent Initiative submitted by ASI. The association criticizes it because, in its view, it would produce an even more pronounced increase in rents. The distinction between proposal, counterproposal and ongoing contract serves to avoid confusing the national debate with the situation of a single household. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## Practical checks for tenants The national percentage is not enough to assess the rent for a single household. For an orderly check, it is advisable to separate the ASI data from the checks on the contract and the federal tenancy rules, which are the same in all Cantons. ### Four checks to carry out 1. Organize the data. Gather the lease, the latest rent statements and the family’s gross income. If the income does not exceed 4'000 francs, compare the share allocated to rent with the 37,8% indicated by ASI. The comparison does not by itself establish a new rent, but it makes the burden on the budget measurable. To read the items in busta paga svizzera, use the amounts actually shown in your documents. 2. Check the cited rate. The source recalls that rents are indexed by law to the reference interest rate and indicates 1,25% as the current level. Compare the rate reported in the documentation with the rent charged. The ASI text does not provide a formula for turning the national figure into an individual rent: therefore, avoid automatically deriving a request from the percentage alone. 3. Check the deposit. In Swiss tenancy, the security deposit may not exceed three months’ rent and must be paid into a blocked account in the tenant’s name. This check concerns the security for the contract, not the general trend of the rent index. 4. Check any termination notice. The landlord’s termination notice is valid only on the official cantonal form. If it is contested, the deadline is 30 days before the conciliation authority. Keeping the form and noting the date of receipt helps ensure that the deadline is met. When following public proposals, note separately whether they concern cost-based rent, Lex Koller or public-utility housing: these are three distinct demands by ASI. To link the burden of housing to monthly income, use calcolatore stipendio. *Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/associazione-inquilini-lancia-allarme-su-prezzi-affitti/92166278)*

item.title: Seventy francs for nine hours of work: the protest
item.description: Uber drivers in Switzerland denounce worsening conditions and demand greater rights and protections. Amid low fares and Bolt's arrival.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 70 francs after nine hours for a driver in Zurich - Before: 1'200 francs for about 30 hours a week - Bolt entered the Zurich market in 2024 - The Federal Supreme Court confirmed the decision in 2023 ## Key facts - Main subject → Cem Kurun, an Uber driver in the Canton of Zurich since 2019 - Current earnings → just over 300 francs - Disputed price → 10 cents above Uber's per-kilometre rate - SECO position → drivers to be classified as employees in 2018 - Geneva → majority of drivers hired through a third-party company After nine hours of work, Cem Kurun had earned 70 francs. The thirty-year-old has driven for Uber in the Canton of Zurich since 2019 and says that, in the meantime, his conditions have worsened: lower fares and more intense competition between private transport services and taxi drivers. The drivers are asking the Swiss authorities for greater rights and protections. Kurun says that in the past he managed to earn 1'200 francs by working about 30 hours a week. Today he earns just over 300 francs. He links the worsening situation to the Covid pandemic and the arrival of Bolt, Uber's Estonian competitor, in the Zurich market in 2024. In his view, many drivers are forced to rely on social assistance. ### Fares and algorithm The dispute concerns not only the amount earned. Kurun claims to have little effective control over the work, even though he operates as an independent driver. He doubts that the app is truly neutral in assigning rides: he says that those who refuse too many rides risk being penalized; areas with higher earnings supposedly appear on the map and then disappear when the driver arrives. The app theoretically allows drivers to set their own price. Kurun claims, however, that if he raises it by just 10 cents above Uber's per-kilometre rate, he stops receiving rides. Uber rejects this interpretation and maintains that drivers can accept or reject rides without penalties. The company also denies that acceptance and cancellation rates are used to match drivers and passengers or to personalize fares. ### The status issue The classification of the employment relationship has been disputed for years. Unia, Switzerland's largest trade union, considers the control exercised by Uber incompatible with genuine independence. According to the union, drivers should receive wages, expense reimbursement and social contributions as employees. SECO had supported this classification as early as 2018, a position confirmed by cantonal and federal court rulings. In Geneva, after a long legal battle, Uber changed its model: today, the majority of drivers are employed through a third-party company, and the group agreed with the canton to pay outstanding social contributions for the preceding period. In Zurich, by contrast, the Social Insurance Court recognized in 2021 the employee status of drivers who use several Uber services; the Federal Supreme Court confirmed this in 2023. Kurun nevertheless maintains that conditions have not improved for him. ## Beyond the fare: the impact on work The case shows why the dispute over independent status is not merely contractual. When the work is presented as self-employed, the driver remains subject to fares, ride assignments, and the app's rules. When the driver is recognized as an employee, Unia argues that wages, reimbursement of expenses, and social contributions must also be taken into account. The difference can weigh on disposable income and on costo della vita in Svizzera: Kurun links current earnings to the inability to support a family and says that some drivers turn to social assistance. The social-security aspect helps explain why the classification matters beyond an individual ride. The social contributions referred to in the dispute can also be understood through AVS/AHV and, when the requirements are met, LPP/BVG. The minimum wage is not the lever described in the source: the dispute concerns the classification of the relationship, the control exercised by the platform, and the protections that Unia associates with employment. To follow this aspect, one can consult the AVS/LPP guide, without confusing the value of a ride with total remuneration. ### Geneva and Zurich as two different signals | Canton | Documented element | Practical interpretation | |---|---|---| | Geneva | Model modified; majority employed through a third-party company | Agreement with the canton concerning outstanding social contributions | | Zurich | 2021 decision, confirmed in 2023 | Kurun maintains that conditions have not improved | The comparison between the cantons avoids a mistake: a judgment does not automatically amount to an identical change for all drivers. In Geneva, the model was changed after the legal battle and the majority of drivers are employed through a third-party company. In Zurich, by contrast, the court decision coexists with Kurun's report of worsening conditions. The transition from legal recognition to actual conditions therefore remains an open question. Uber says it has changed its model several times and that the judgments concern arrangements that are no longer current. It champions the independence and flexibility valued by the majority and cites free insurance coverage against certain risks for independent driver-partners in Switzerland. The practical test concerns the actual freedom to set the price, reject rides, and continue receiving them: on this point, the platform and drivers remain at odds. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## A concrete check for those who drive via an app The most solid way to turn the problem into a documented complaint is to separate four elements: time worked, money collected, app rules, and the nature of the relationship. The source does not indicate a national form or a single deadline; therefore, it is better not to add procedures that are not documented. The practical path can start from the data already cited in the investigation. ### Four useful steps 1. Reconstruct the days. For each day, record hours, earnings, rides received, and fare applied. Comparing the result after nine hours with that obtained by working about 30 hours a week helps distinguish a weak day from a broader trend. These numbers remain a personal record, not an official hourly wage. 2. Verify actual freedom. Keep the price settings, rejected or canceled rides, and screenshots of zones that promise higher earnings. If a zone disappears upon arrival or rides stop after a minimal change to the fare, the data should be separated from the interpretation: Kurun considers it a penalty, while Uber denies that penalties exist. 3. Identify the contractual model. It is necessary to distinguish the activity described as independent from employment through a third-party company, which is currently indicated for the majority of drivers in Geneva. This check prevents confusing the Geneva model with the one reported by a driver in the Canton of Zurich. To organize the financial items, you can use the guide to busta paga svizzera, without turning the link into automatic proof of status. 4. Separate the claims. Wages, professional expenses, and social contributions are different items. Guillaume Lemoine said that he had taken legal action against Uber to recover sums he believes were unpaid; the dispute is still ongoing. Anyone reconstructing their own position should therefore state precisely which item they are contesting and keep communications with the platform. The source also shows that drivers are asking the Swiss authorities for greater rights and protections, but it does not replace an individual proceeding. The checklist serves to move from a generic complaint to a readable picture: hours, amounts, fare, rides, contractual model, and contested item. item.title: Three Ticino companies in the Top100 Swiss Startup Award 2026
item.description: InkVivo, Jaipur Robotics, and In Virtuo Laboratories represent Ticino in the ranking of the one hundred most promising Swiss startups of 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Three Ticino companies enter the Top100 Swiss Startup Award 2026 - InkVivo and In Virtuo work on drugs in Lugano - Jaipur Robotics develops AI for waste facilities - Jaipur's team collaborates with more than 35 European facilities ## Key facts - Recognition → Top100 Swiss Startup Award 2026 - Companies → InkVivo Technologies, Jaipur Robotics, In Virtuo Laboratories - Locations → Lugano and Manno - Team → InkVivo 7 people; Jaipur about 40; In Virtuo around ten LUGANO - InkVivo Technologies SA, Jaipur Robotics AG and In Virtuo Laboratories SA, all based in Ticino, have been included among the one hundred most promising Swiss startups according to the Top100 Swiss Startup Award 2026. The recognition is presented as the country’s most authoritative award dedicated to young innovative companies. The three companies operate in pharmaceuticals, waste and artificial intelligence. ### The three companies in the ranking InkVivo Technologies, based in Piazza Cioccaro in Lugano, develops polymer platforms for formulating drug delivery systems. Elia Guzzi, CEO and co-founder, describes a technology designed to control where and for how long active ingredients are released in the body. > «We develop new drugs using technologies that make it possible to control where and for how long active ingredients are released in the body,» explains Elia Guzzi. At their core are proprietary polymers and Machine Learning, used to accelerate formulation development and aim for greater bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy. The two internal programs concern iron-deficiency anemia, already in the clinical phase with ETH Zurich and FFHS, and Alzheimer’s, still in the preclinical phase. The company has seven employees and also collaborates with SUPSI-IDSIA. Guzzi founded InkVivo with Leonardo Tognola and Stefano Cerutti after completing his doctorate at ETH Zurich. Jaipur Robotics AG has offices in Manno and develops computer vision and artificial intelligence solutions for waste-to-energy plants and industrial facilities. The system analyzes waste in real time, flags non-compliant objects, helps trace them back to the supplier and provides guidance on mixing, combustion, calorific value, emissions and crane control. Estimated savings reach up to 5 million francs per year for a plant. Ermes Zamboni and Nikhil Prakash met at ETH Zurich; after the first plant in Bellinzona, the company now collaborates with more than 35 facilities in Europe. The team numbers about 40 people. In Virtuo Laboratories SA, also based in Lugano, develops artificial intelligence methods and molecular simulations for drug discovery. Its tools are used to predict how a potential drug binds to its target before synthesis in the laboratory, so that molecules that are not very effective or may have unwanted effects can be discarded in advance. The company was founded in 2024 out of Gianvito Grasso’s work as a researcher at IDSIA (USI-SUPSI) and develops therapeutic programs independently or with industrial partners. The team consists of around ten people. ## Concrete implications of the ranking The source provides mainly industrial data: three Ticino sites, pharmaceutical programs at different stages, a system for waste-to-energy plants connected to facilities in Europe, and teams of different sizes. It does not, however, report salaries, open positions, investments, taxes or new regulations. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the ranking should therefore be read as a snapshot of activities and expertise, not as an automatic promise of employment or income. ### Three useful indicators | Company | Stated focus | Measurable signal in the source | | InkVivo | Controlled drug release | Anemia in the clinical phase; Alzheimer's in the preclinical phase | | Jaipur Robotics | Computer vision and AI for waste | More than 35 facilities in Europe; estimated savings of up to 5 million francs per year per facility | | In Virtuo | AI and molecular simulations | Own programs and programs with industrial partners | The first indicator is the distance between research and application. InkVivo connects materials and Machine Learning to two programs at different stages of maturity. In Virtuo operates before synthesis, using simulations and artificial intelligence methods to select the molecules to be evaluated. The comparison shows that the word startup covers different operational stages: from preclinical or clinical research to the development of methods for reducing laboratory steps. The second indicator is the industrial use already described for Jaipur Robotics. The company does not merely classify waste: the system flags non-compliant objects, traces them back to the supplier and supports decisions on mixing, combustion, emissions and cranes. For those observing the Swiss economy, the reference to the first Bellinzona facility and European collaborations links a Ticino site to an activity that extends beyond cantonal boundaries. The third indicator is the network. InkVivo works with ETH Zurich, FFHS and SUPSI-IDSIA; In Virtuo also develops programs with industrial partners; Jaipur brings together expertise in artificial intelligence, robotics and waste management, with work spanning Europe and Asia. These are useful elements for understanding where activities are located, but they are not enough to infer hiring, salaries or investments. Those looking for a professional starting point can compare aziende che assumono and annunci di lavoro, using the ranking to select the sectors to explore further. The source, however, does not report open positions: the step from the news to an application therefore requires a separate check. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## Operational steps for the reader The ranking can be used as a verification framework, without attributing to it information that the source does not contain. The practical goal is to separate sector, location, project maturity, and team size before seeking further data. ### A four-step procedure 1. Define the area. For pharmaceuticals, distinguish InkVivo's controlled release from In Virtuo's methods, which predict how a potential drug binds to its target before synthesis. For industry, consider Jaipur Robotics and applications in waste-to-energy plants. 2. Note locations and connections. InkVivo and In Virtuo are in Lugano; Jaipur Robotics is in Manno. The stated references include ETH Zurich, FFHS, SUPSI-IDSIA, the first plant in Bellinzona, and more than 35 plants in Europe. The map helps distinguish research, technological development, and industrial application. 3. Consider the team size. Available data indicate seven people at InkVivo, about 40 at Jaipur Robotics, and around ten at In Virtuo. Use them to compare the stated organizational size, not to automatically infer roles, hiring, or working conditions. 4. Verify the project phase. InkVivo's iron-deficiency anemia is in the clinical phase, Alzheimer's is in the preclinical phase, while In Virtuo works on selecting potential drugs and Jaipur on plants and waste. This distinction avoids treating a clinical phase, preclinical research, and an industrial solution as equivalent. ### From reading to research At this point, one can move from areas to opportunities: consult the annunci di lavoro and compare the aziende che assumono, looking for the sector consistent with the skills mentioned in the profile.
