item.title: Pellet prices in Ticino: price increases and winter purchases
item.description: Analysis of pellet prices in Ticino with estimated price increases between 5% and 10% and recommendations for purchases before winter.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - PelleTicino reports an increase of approximately 5%. - Thermocentro indicates prices approximately 10% higher. - In October, the supplier reports 40 francs more per tonne. - The recommendation: buy before winter.
## Key facts - Company → PelleTicino SA, based in Biasca - Origin → local and 100% Ticino production - PelleTicino increase → approximately 5% compared with last year - Thermocentro increase → approximately 10% compared with last year - October → approximately 40 francs more per tonne
### The increase and its causes
In Biasca, PelleTicino SA is facing the heating season with a pellet price higher than last year's. Lorenzo Zanetti, co-founder and member of the Board of Directors, explains that for his company the increase is around 5%. The young company, specializing in the production of local, 100% Ticino wood pellets, is currently able to maintain a competitive price thanks to direct production.
The indications are not uniform, however. Zanetti reports that even higher increases can be found on the market. He puts diesel at the top of the list of causes, as its price has risen considerably. Transport affects the final price, especially when the pellets travel long distances. This is also why, he explains, importers end up offering such high prices per bag.
For those who need to stock up before winter, the forecast cannot be certain. The trend in the raw material nevertheless suggests further increases in the winter months. Zanetti's recommendation is therefore clear: «it is advisable to buy now». The current price charged by PelleTicino is communicated to customers without any guarantee that it will remain unchanged between December and March.
A similar picture emerges from S. Antonino, where Dario Previti heads Thermocentro Service SA. Previti confirms the increase and urges people not to create alarm: compared with last year, prices are currently approximately 10% higher. For October, the company's supplier indicated an increase of approximately 40 francs per tonne. Here too, the energy required for production and above all transport play a role, compounded by the sharp rise in diesel prices.
Between health insurance, petrol and galloping inflation, heating becomes another expense to consider for those keeping an eye on costo della vita in Svizzera before the cold weather arrives. The source reports that buying in summer tends to be more advantageous, while as demand increases the product may cost more. Thermocentro does not expect supply problems: Previti explains that its storage capacity allows it to guarantee supplies to its customers. Finally, there is an invitation to check the certifications, even when they entail a slightly higher expense, because they provide a certain calorific value and help preserve the health of the stove or boiler. ## How to read price signals
The comparison between the two companies requires care. The 5% reported by PelleTicino and the approximately 10% indicated for Thermocentro describe two separate figures: the source does not present them as a single increase to be added together. The unit of measurement also changes. The October figure is expressed in francs per tonne, while the assessment of cost-effectiveness compared with heating oil concerns the price per bag.
### Price, transport and purchase period
| Indication | Practical interpretation | |---|---| | approximately 5% | increase reported by PelleTicino compared with last year | | approximately 10% | price level reported by Thermocentro compared with last year | | approximately 40 francs per tonne | increase indicated by the supplier for October | | more than 7 francs per bag | according to the operator, pellets remain cost-effective compared with heating oil |
The distinction between direct production and imports is decisive in understanding the final price. PelleTicino links its competitive price to direct production. For importers, on the other hand, long-distance transport affects the cost to the customer. When examining an offer, the figure should therefore be considered together with the origin of the pellets and the logistics component, without confusing the price per bag with that per tonne.
The calendar adds a second element. Summer is indicated as the period that tends to be most affordable; as the cold arrives, demand increases and the product may become more expensive. Anyone postponing the purchase should bear in mind that PelleTicino's current price is not guaranteed between December and March. The figure provided by Thermocentro's supplier for October offers a further signal of the possible increase in cost per tonne, not a certainty valid for every purchase.
The comparison with heating oil changes the way the price is viewed: according to the operator, pellets remain cost-effective even above 7 francs per bag. However, the source also encourages looking at certifications. Spending a little more may mean having a guarantee of a given calorific value and a product that helps preserve the health of the stove or boiler.
The reassurance regarding supplies concerns Thermocentro and its customers, thanks to the storage capacity stated by Previti. To compare the expected expenditure with monthly income, the comparison can be paired with a reading of busta paga svizzera, keeping the fuel price, purchase period and product characteristics separate.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to organize the purchase
The information gathered makes it possible to carry out a concrete check before restocking. The periods to keep in mind are summer, October and the months between December and March: summer is described as a generally more convenient period, October is associated with the supplier's forecast, while for the colder months PelleTicino does not guarantee the current price.
### Four checks before choosing
1. Act before the cold weather. If the pellet is needed for winter, the source indicates that buying in summer tends to cost less. Those who have not yet done so are encouraged to act in good time, without waiting for demand to rise during the colder months.
2. Ask which price applies today and read it as a snapshot, not as a promise for the entire season. PelleTicino communicates the current price to customers, but does not guarantee that it will remain unchanged between December and March. The figure of about 40 francs more per tonne indicated by the supplier for October should be kept separate from that price.
3. Compare the size of the offer. For bags, the reference reported by the source is pellet that is still convenient compared with heating oil even above 7 francs per bag. For supplies by the tonne, on the other hand, the expected increase indicated for October must be taken into account. In both cases, transport over long distances may affect the final price.
4. Check the certifications and the stated availability. Certification may cost a little more, but it provides guarantees regarding heating value and the condition of the stove or boiler. For Thermocentro, storage capacity is indicated as sufficient to guarantee supplies to customers.
Once these elements have been collected, keep the price, unit of sale, stated validity period and certification together. This way, the comparison remains clear even if the product changes price with the cold weather or if you switch from an importer to direct production. The source does not make it possible to predict prices with certainty, but it does make it possible to avoid two mistakes: postponing the purchase without considering the increase in demand and choosing based solely on the price, while ignoring transport and certifications.
To track the weight of this expense in costo della vita in Svizzera, compare the price of pellet with other recurring expenses. To relate heating expenses to monthly income, use calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

## TL;DR - In the Canton of Bern, cantonal rules and offices apply. - Calculation, payment and deadlines must be checked against the official source. - Changes of vehicle and address require an up-to-date check. - The operational point of reference is the road traffic office. ## Key facts - Territory → Canton of Bern - Area → motor vehicle tax - Checks → criteria, requirements, deadlines and amounts - Changes → change of vehicle and address update - Reference → road traffic office In the Canton of Bern, motor vehicle tax follows a cantonal framework: calculation, payment, deadlines, change of vehicle and address update are matters to be handled according to the rules and offices of the canton. For anyone who has to manage the procedure, the consequence is direct: requirements, deadlines and amounts must be checked against the official source of the Canton of Bern. The road traffic office is the operational point of reference indicated for this matter. Verification of the calculation must be read together with the instructions on payment, deadlines and changes reported for the change of vehicle and the address update. ### A jurisdiction not to be confused The Swiss tax framework provides for three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; for municipalities, the multiplier is applied to the cantonal tax. This distinction helps explain why the competent office matters, but on its own does not provide the criterion for motor vehicle tax in the Canton of Bern. For this service, the source expressly indicates cantonal rules and offices. AFC/ESTV manages direct federal tax and VAT. Cantonal administrations manage cantonal and municipal tax. UFAS/BSV concerns social security, including AVS/AI/LPP, and does not set taxes; UST/BFS produces statistics and does not set tax rates. These are different areas of responsibility, which should not be conflated when looking for the point of contact for motor vehicle tax. For this reason, a consultation on dichiarazione delle imposte must remain separate from verification of motor vehicle tax. The former belongs to the general tax framework; the latter must be traced back to the cantonal indications on calculation, payment, deadlines and updates. The principle also applies to anyone who changes vehicle or address: it is not enough to retain the procedure used previously. The change is among the steps to be checked with the road traffic office, while requirements, deadlines and amounts remain anchored to the canton’s official source. ## What changes in practical handling The most concrete consequence of cantonal jurisdiction concerns how the case is assessed. The starting point is not a figure taken from another territory, but the criterion applicable in the Canton of Bern. The source calls for verifying requirements, deadlines and amounts with the canton: first the situation is identified, then which official guidance describes it is checked. A figure from another canton cannot be treated as confirmation for Bern, because motor vehicle tax is governed by cantonal rules and handled by cantonal offices. ### From the ordinary case to changes In a hypothetical ordinary-payment scenario, the logical process is straightforward: the cantonal criterion is checked, the relevant deadline is identified, and the amount indicated for that case is checked. There is no need to turn the general tax system into a formula for the car: the three levels of the Swiss tax system remain an institutional distinction, while the motor vehicle levy should be interpreted according to the canton’s guidance. Changing the vehicle calls for a different check. The source lists it alongside calculation, payment and deadlines; therefore, anyone who changes the vehicle should not automatically reuse a previous check. It is necessary to check how the road traffic office handles the change and which requirements, deadlines and amounts are associated with the new case. Updating the address follows the same administrative logic, but should not be confused with changing the vehicle. In a hypothetical scenario in which the two changes coincide, it is prudent to carry out two separate checks against the official source and the office’s guidance, without assuming that one update replaces the other. | Situation | What to check | Reference | | Calculation | Applicable criteria | Official source of the Canton of Bern | | Payment | Deadline and amount for the case | Official source of the canton | | Change of vehicle | Requirements and the required update | Road traffic office | | Address | Update procedure | Road traffic office | The table separates four stages that are often combined: knowing how it is calculated is not equivalent to knowing the payment deadline, and having updated an address does not demonstrate that the vehicle change has also been checked. For a broader view of household expenses, costo della vita in Svizzera may be used alongside it, without using it in place of the official cantonal source. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Practical procedure Management becomes simpler if the verification is broken down into short steps. The source does not replace the instructions of the Canton of Bern: it serves to establish which office to consult and which information to check. ### The operational sequence 1. Define the procedure. Determine whether you need to verify the calculation, proceed with payment, manage a vehicle change, or update your address. If there are multiple needs, note them down separately: these are variations mentioned by the source. 2. Start from the official source of the Canton. Look for instructions regarding the criteria, requirements, deadlines, and amounts of the motor vehicle tax. These are the elements that the source entrusts to cantonal rules; do not replace them with a deadline or an amount obtained from another Canton. 3. Use the motor vehicle office as an operational reference. When the procedure involves a vehicle change or an address update, check with this office which update is required and in what form it must be followed. The procedure to apply is the one indicated by the competent cantonal authority. 4. Keep jurisdictions separate. FTA/ESTV deals with direct federal tax and VAT; cantonal administrations manage cantonal and municipal taxes. FSIO/BSV deals with social security, including AHV/IV/BVG, while FSO/BFS deals with statistics. For the motor vehicle tax, the path to follow remains the cantonal one. 5. Complete the check before payment. Double-check that the deadline and amount are the ones published for the procedure in the Canton of Bern. If your vehicle or address has changed in the meantime, repeat the check on requirements and updates instead of assuming the previous consultation is still valid. This sequence avoids mixing up a motor vehicle procedure with the general tax return, social security, or statistics. It also keeps the question on calculation separate from the one on payment: for both, the verification must be completed in the official cantonal source and at the competent office. This rule is simple to apply even at the national level: when a service is administered by the Cantons, requirements, deadlines, and amounts must be sought from the canton concerned. In the case of Bern, the final check must therefore remain anchored to the official cantonal information and the motor vehicle office. item.description: In the Canton of Bern, social assistance is based on need: application to the competent office, documents, and deadlines to be verified with the Canton.

## TL;DR - Social assistance is based on need. - Cantons and municipalities generally administer it. - In Bern, the office, documents and deadlines must be checked. ## Key facts - Criterion → need - Administration → Cantons and municipalities - Application → competent municipal or cantonal office - Verification → official source of the Canton of Bern In the Canton of Bern, social assistance is generally administered by Cantons and municipalities according to need. For anyone who has to submit an application, the first point of reference is therefore the competent municipal or cantonal office; requirements, documents, deadlines and amounts must be verified using the official source of the Canton. ### The criterion of need The stated criterion is a situation of need, with administration organized at cantonal and municipal level. For this reason, the application must be addressed to the office handling the case, without replacing the procedure with generic information taken from other areas of public administration. The office’s specific authority, together with the required documentation, must be checked before submission. The main federal bodies also have distinct responsibilities. UFAS/BSV concerns social security, including AVS/AHV, AI and LPP/BVG; UST/BFS produces statistics and does not set rates. AFC/ESTV deals with direct federal tax and VAT, while cantonal administrations manage cantonal and municipal taxation. This separation helps prevent an application for social assistance from being confused with a tax, social security or statistical matter. ### Items affecting the budget LAMal/KVG is another separate matter to keep in mind: for residents, health insurance is mandatory and must be taken out within three months of arrival. Premiums are per capita, vary according to canton and region, and are neither a tax nor a wage contribution; premium reduction is a cantonal subsidy. The guide to cassa malati is available for further information on the insurance aspect. The general framework therefore remains clear: social assistance is linked to need, ordinary administration is handled by Cantons and municipalities, and the application is initiated at the competent office. The operational rules to use for Bern are those published by the Canton, especially to understand which documents to submit and by what deadlines. There is no need to automatically transfer into the application the rules governing direct federal tax, AVS/AHV or LAMal/KVG: these are different systems, with different authorities and purposes. Within the framework described, the word requirements does not refer to a single list to be applied indiscriminately. It identifies the conditions and checks associated with the competent channel in the Canton. The same applies to the application: the point of access is municipal or cantonal, while the practical framework is defined by the office and the official source of Bern. For those living in the Canton of Bern, the difference between the various channels changes how the budget is prepared, but does not replace the needs-based criterion. In a hypothetical scenario, a person who cannot cover their expenses must distinguish at least three areas: financial hardship, insurance premiums and social deductions from their salary. Confusing them may lead to contacting the wrong office or using amounts belonging to another system. ### Disposable income and benefits do not coincide If the person works, the payslip lists separate items. AVS/AI/IPG amount to 5.3% for the employee and 10.6% overall including the employer. AD/AC is indicated at 1.1% up to the annual ceiling, while LAINF/LAA varies from 0.7% to 1.5% depending on the sector. For LPP/BVG, on the coordinated salary, the indicated rates are 7% between the ages of 25 and 34, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54 and 18% from age 55 until the reference age. These are items to be considered separately from social assistance. The guide to busta paga svizzera can be used to compare deductions. In the personal budget, LAMal/KVG must also be recorded as a separate item. It is mandatory for residents, provides per-capita premiums differentiated by canton and region, and is neither a tax nor a payroll contribution. The reduction in premiums is a cantonal subsidy. This distinction avoids confusing an insurance cost with an application for social assistance, without anticipating which requirements are applied by the competent office. Taxation also follows a separate logic: in Switzerland there are three levels, direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each Canton has its own law and its own multiplier; the municipality applies the multiplier to the cantonal tax. AFC/ESTV concerns direct federal tax and VAT, while the cantonal administrations handle cantonal and municipal taxes. This information serves to classify an item correctly and reconstruct expenses, not to replace the social assistance channel. Comparing with costo della vita in Svizzera can help organize expenses, provided that each item remains linked to its own system. The application, however, continues to depend on the financial hardship and the procedure of the competent municipal or cantonal office. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. A well-organized application is built by following the scope indicated by the Canton, without replacing it with a standard list valid everywhere. The process can be divided into four steps: identify the office, verify the conditions, prepare the required documents, and comply with the cooperation obligations. ### From verification to submission 1. Identify the point of access. For the Canton of Bern, the relevant contact is the competent municipal or cantonal office. Before submitting the request, check which of the two channels handles the case and use the contact details published by the Canton's official source. 2. Check the scope. The condition of need is the criterion specified for social assistance. On the official source, verify the applicable requirements, deadlines, documents, and amounts. Do not use figures taken from another Canton or from a different year. 3. Prepare the documentation. Providing the required documents is part of cooperating with the office. The procedure is not completed by replacing the official list with a generic template: each document must be selected based on the instructions received and submitted within the prescribed deadline. 4. Keep the related channels separate. If you are a resident, LAMal/KVG must be taken out within three months of arrival; the premium reduction is a cantonal subsidy. The AVS/AHV, AI, LPP/BVG, and AD/AC items that appear on the payslip help assess the budget, but do not turn the application into a social security or tax procedure. The verification of figures requires caution. The maximum amounts for pillar 3a, the threshold and coordination deduction for LPP, the AD/AC maximum, average LAMal premiums, and the median salary are indexed every year. When the application requires an up-to-date financial overview, it is preferable to verify the year indicated by the official source instead of reporting uncertain amounts. The same principle applies to any cantonal rules on benefits and services: requirements, deadlines, and amounts must be checked at Canton level. This method keeps the channels separate and directs the request to the indicated office, with documents and checks in line with cantonal rules. item.title: Minimum wage in the Canton of Bern: requirements and application
item.description: In Switzerland there is no federal minimum: in Bern, any applicable cantonal rules, collective agreements and official checks are what matter.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In Switzerland, there is no federal minimum wage. - Some cantons have their own minimum wage. - A collective agreement must be distinguished from the cantonal minimum. - Requirements and amounts must be verified against the cantonal source. ## Key facts - Federal level → no federal minimum wage - Cantonal level → some cantons have their own minimum - Maximum working hours → 45 or 50 hours per week - Minimum vacation → 4 weeks, 5 for those under 20 - Notice period → 1, 2 or 3 months depending on length of service ### The federal rule Switzerland does not have a federal minimum wage. This is the starting point for anyone working in the Canton of Bern: there is no national figure to apply automatically to every employment relationship. However, the national framework specifies that some cantons have their own minimum wage. The review must therefore distinguish the federal rule from any cantonal provisions. For Bern, the practical question is not only how much one earns, but which rule covers the employment relationship. The sector concerned, the applicable requirements, any cantonal application, the inspections, and the office indicated by the canton’s official source must be verified. Without an official indication, a rule from another canton cannot be turned into a Bernese rule, nor can an amount, an effective date, or a single threshold be specified. ### Cantonal minimum and collective agreement The second level concerns collective agreements. Where there is no cantonal minimum, wage rules may differ from those of a minimum established at cantonal level: the collective agreement is therefore a document to examine in order to determine whether the work falls under its rules. The two categories are not synonyms. The worker must compare the cantonal situation with the applicable agreement, avoiding the deduction of rights from a figure found online or referring to another canton. The general employment framework nevertheless contains useful national parameters. The maximum working week is 45 hours in industry, offices, and sales, and 50 hours in other sectors. The minimum vacation entitlement is four weeks, rising to five for those under 20. Notice periods also follow a schedule of one, two, or three months: one in the first year, two from the second to the ninth, and three from the tenth. These elements do not replace verification of the minimum wage, but they help put the employment relationship in context. To check how the salary is presented and which items appear, this review can be supplemented with the guide on busta paga svizzera. ## From the threshold to the budget Any potential minimum wage in the Canton of Bern should be considered together with the deductions and costs that affect the budget. The salary amount alone does not describe monthly disposable income: social contributions follow their own rules, while LAMal is separate from salary. ### From the salary amount to the deductions The contribution table provided by the source is as follows: | Item | Rule | | --- | --- | | AVS/AI/IPG | 5.3% paid by the employee; 10.6% overall including the employer | | AD/AC | 1.1% up to the annual maximum | | LAINF/LAA | 0.7–1.5% depending on the sector | | LPP | on the coordinated salary: 7% (25–34), 10% (35–44), 15% (45–54), 18% (55+ up to the reference age) | | LAMal | mandatory for residents; per capita premium, not a tax or salary contribution | This distinction is especially useful to avoid confusing the minimum wage with net pay. The AD/AC figure is linked to an annual maximum, while LPP is expressed as a percentage of the coordinated salary and varies by age bracket. LAINF/LAA varies according to the sector. Without the complete picture, it is not possible to derive a single net amount from a gross figure. ### Taxes and cost of living Taxes also follow three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; in municipalities, the multiplier is applied to the cantonal tax. Therefore, salary comparisons must keep salary, contributions and taxes separate, without presenting a deduction as if it were a component of the minimum wage. LAMal works differently. It is mandatory for residents and must be taken out within three months of arrival; it is private, with per capita premiums, and is neither a tax nor a salary contribution. Premiums depend on the canton and region, while premium reductions are a cantonal subsidy. This is why costo della vita in Svizzera and LAMal/cassa malati should be assessed separately from checking the salary. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Procedure for the Canton of Bern For anyone who needs to check how it is applied in the Canton of Bern, the most prudent approach is to start at the level of the rule and only then move on to the payslip. This sequence avoids using amounts or offices taken from another Canton. ### 1. Define the question Establish whether you need to verify a cantonal minimum wage, a requirement, the sector concerned, an inspection or a collective agreement. The first answer to keep in mind is national: there is no federal minimum wage. Therefore, the research must focus on any rules specific to the Canton and the employment relationship concerned. ### 2. Use the official source of the Canton Look in the official cantonal source for information on application, requirements, amounts, deadlines, inspections and the competent office. These are precisely the data that cannot be replaced with generic information about the Cantons. If the page concerns another territory, do not use it as evidence for Bern. ### 3. Check the collective agreement separately If no applicable cantonal minimum emerges, check the relevant collective agreement. The collective agreement and the cantonal minimum remain distinct levels: the former must not be presented as a federal threshold, and the latter cannot be derived automatically from a collective rule. ### 4. Read the salary together with the related items Compare the salary figure with the social security items on the payslip. AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA and LPP have different bases or rates; LAMal, on the other hand, remains a separate per-capita premium. For the tax part, remember that AFC/ESTV handles IFD and VAT, while the cantonal administrations manage the cantonal and municipal levels. This distinction helps direct the request to the correct authority. ### 5. Verify personal obligations Anyone residing in Switzerland must take out LAMal within three months of arrival. For the rest, the requirements, deadlines and amounts of cantonal benefits must be checked against the official source of the Canton. The national minimum wage rule does not replace that check. Once you have gathered the cantonal reference, any applicable collective agreement and the payslip items, you can estimate the effect on the budget without confusing gross pay, contributions, premiums and taxes. To complete the calculation, use calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.title: Continuing education Canton Zurich: requirements and contributions
item.description: In the Canton of Zurich, recognized programs, requirements, deadlines and contributions must be verified at the official cantonal source.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In the Canton of Zurich, cantonal rules apply - Requirements and deadlines must be checked against the official source - Contribution amounts should be checked with the Canton - The application goes through the competent office or institution ## Key facts - Scope → continuing education in the Canton of Zurich - To be verified → recognized programs, requirements, deadlines, amounts - Responsibility → Cantons and cantonal offices - AFC/ESTV → direct federal tax and VAT - UFAS/BSV → AVS/AI/LPP - UST/BFS → statistics Contributions for continuing education follow cantonal rules and offices. In the Canton of Zurich, therefore, application requirements, deadlines and amounts must be checked in the canton’s official source. ### The scope of responsibility The search for a recognized program must focus on the education program in question and on the information published by the cantonal office or competent institution. The source does not provide a list of courses, an income threshold or a single deadline to apply to the Canton of Zurich. Presenting one of these elements as a general rule would mean going beyond the verified data. The choice of authority also requires care. AFC/ESTV deals with direct federal tax and VAT. Cantonal administrations manage cantonal and municipal matters. UFAS/BSV concerns social security, including AVS, AI and LPP, while UST/BFS produces statistics and does not set rates. These bodies do not replace the cantonal source to be consulted for an application for a continuing education contribution. The distinction is also useful for budgeting. The Swiss tax system includes direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax; each canton has its own law and multiplier, with the municipality applying the multiplier to the cantonal tax. This tax framework, by itself, does not indicate whether an educational program is recognized or whether an application is admissible. The cantonal process does not mean that every element of the Swiss system is cantonal. The division of responsibilities remains clear: the official source should be used for the training measure, while tax and social security data should be consulted with the authority responsible for each area. This separation prevents statistical information or a payslip item from being turned into an admission requirement. Anyone who needs to assess the impact of training on their budget can supplement the administrative check with costo della vita in Svizzera, without replacing the official Canton of Zurich page. ## What changes in the practical verification The concrete consequence is that the application must be built in two distinct steps: first, the cantonal measure is identified, and then the conditions indicated by the competent authority are checked. It is not advisable to use an amount read in a national guide or a figure belonging to another sector as a reference. For continuing education, the correct comparison remains with the official source of the canton. ### Separating areas before doing the math | Item | Reference | |---|---| | Continuing education contributions | Cantonal rules and offices | | Direct Federal Tax and VAT | FTA/ESTV | | AHV, IV and BVG/LPP | FSIO/BSV | | Statistics | FSO/BFS | The table avoids confusing authorities, values and procedures. Figures indexed annually, such as the third pillar 3a maximum, the BVG/LPP coordination threshold or deduction, the ALC maximum, the average LAMal/KVG premiums and the median salary, are not a price list for continuing education contributions. If they do not refer to the cantonal measure, they do not allow deriving either the recognizable amount or the application deadline. Disposable income also requires separate reading. AHV/IV/EO contributions are 5.3% for the employee and 10.6% in total with the employer; ALC is 1.1% up to the annual maximum and UVG/LAA varies from 0.7% to 1.5% according to the sector. BVG/LPP on the coordinated salary provides for 7% between 25 and 34 years of age, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54 and 18% from 55 years up to the reference age. These are items to be read in the Swiss payslip, not substitutes for cantonal requirements. ### Planning the employment relationship LAMal/KVG follows yet another logic: it is mandatory for residents, has per capita premiums and premiums defined by canton or region, but it is neither a tax nor a salary contribution. Separating this expense from the training contribution helps to read the cost of life without adding different items. Work also has general rules to keep distinct. In Switzerland there is no federal minimum wage, although some cantons have their own. The maximum working hours are 45 hours per week in industry, offices and retail, or 50 hours in other sectors; the minimum vacation is four weeks, five for those under 20 years of age. These references describe the employment relationship and do not establish the admissibility of the cantonal application. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Operational procedure for the application To avoid errors, the process must remain anchored to the official source of the Canton of Zurich. The cantonal rule can be turned into a sequence of checks without anticipating requirements, deadlines, or amounts that have not been published by the competent authority. ### Five steps before submission 1. Identify the program and the associated contribution measure. The search must concern the continuing education program in question and the official page describing its recognition. It is not enough to generically associate every course with cantonal support. 2. Read the requirements in the official version. The available source does not indicate a national list of conditions: it is therefore necessary to use the conditions reported for the Canton of Zurich and not transfer criteria from another Canton or another measure. 3. Record the application deadline. There is no national date to substitute for the cantonal deadline. The deadline to follow is the one published by the cantonal office or the institution competent for the procedure in question. 4. Verify the applicable amount. Contribution amounts must be checked against the official source of the canton. Do not use in their place indexed figures relating to the third pillar 3a, LPP, AD/AC, LAMal, or the median salary. 5. Submit the request through the indicated channel. Responsibility for continuing education remains cantonal. If the question instead concerns federal direct tax or VAT, the reference is AFC/ESTV; for AVS, AI, and LPP, it concerns social security, while UST/BFS concerns statistics. After these checks, the financial assessment must also keep the items separate. The cost of living, salary deductions, and LAMal/KVG premiums may affect the personal budget, but they do not replace verification of the recognized program, the requirements, the deadline, and the cantonal amount. The same principle applies to anyone comparing the support with the minimum wage or with the conditions of their employment relationship: these are different matters. The safest procedure is therefore simple: identify the measure, read the official source, note the deadline and amount, then use the indicated office. To complete the verification of disposable income, use the calcolatore stipendio.
